sections.results: Among 665 endovascular repairs, 14 patients developed AGI. Eight patients were treated with CT-guided antibiotic irrigation. Infection resolved in 4 patients (n = 4/8), and 1 patient (n = 1/8) was treated as a bridge to open aortic surgical repair OSR. Persistent infection was observed in 3 patients (3/8). Cumulative mortality was 0% at 30 days (n = 0/8), 13% at 90 days (n = 1/8), and 50% (n = 4/8) at 1 to 3 years. Three patients (n = 3/8) died from recurrent infection. The literature review identified 6 studies, adding 28 cases. All patients were treated with antibiotic irrigation either as primary therapy or as a bridge to OSR. Short-term/30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 22%, except for 1 study, with mortality of 50%. Most studies achieved effective infection control in high-risk surgical candidates.
sections.conclusion: In highly selected groups of patients who are not candidates for extensive surgery such as aortic reconstruction, percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation may be an alternative treatment method.Clinical ImpactAGI after endovascular repair carries high mortality, current guidelines recommendation is endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction. This may not be feasible for frail patients. This single-center case series along with literature review of 6 studies suggest it may be feasible with minimally invasive CT-guided percutaneous drainage with local antibiotic irrigation in carefully selected patients who are unfit for major surgery.

items.title: Debridement Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Diabetic Foot Ulcers With Borderline Infrapopliteal Ischemia: A Prospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) complicated by infrapopliteal peripheral arterial disease (PAD) represent a major cause of morbidity and nontraumatic lower-limb amputation worldwide. In patients with borderline ischemia, the optimal management strategy remains unclear, with some clinicians advocating conservative debridement while others favor early endovascular revascularization. To compare clinical outcomes of conservative management with surgical debridement versus an endovascular-first strategy followed by debridement in patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal PAD.
sections.methods: This prospective nonrandomized study included patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal PAD treated at a tertiary vascular center between March 2020 and March 2024. Patients with ankle-brachial index (ABI) values of 0.5-0.8 or falsely elevated ABI (>1.3) with preserved distal flow were included. Participants were managed with either conservative treatment (surgical debridement alone) or endovascular revascularization followed by debridement. Clinical, anatomical, and radiological assessments included the WIfI classification, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS), and Peripheral Arterial Calcification Scoring System (PACSS). Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics between groups. Primary outcomes included wound healing and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 12 months.
sections.results: A total of 426 patients were analyzed (264 debridement and 162 revascularization). Patients undergoing revascularization had a greater burden of advanced limb disease, with a significantly higher prevalence of WIfI stage IV ulcers (51.9% vs 31.8%, P = .005), more advanced GLASS stage, and higher PACSS grades, whereas baseline cardiovascular comorbidities including hypertension, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, and previous vascular intervention were comparable between groups. After PSM, 2 balanced cohorts of 100 patients each were compared. Amputation-free survival was similar between the debridement and revascularization groups (74% vs 70%, P = .824). Rates of major adverse limb events and overall mortality were also comparable. Multivariate analysis identified wound depth and GLASS stage as strong predictors of major amputation, while direct angiosomal revascularization was associated with improved wound healing and reduced limb-loss risk.
sections.conclusion: In patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal ischemia, conservative management with timely debridement may achieve outcomes comparable with endovascular revascularization. Anatomical disease severity and wound characteristics appear to be stronger determinants of prognosis than the choice of revascularization strategy.Clinical ImpactThis study highlights the importance of individualized treatment selection in patients with diabetic foot ulcers and borderline infrapopliteal ischemia. Wound depth and anatomical disease complexity should be carefully considered when determining the need for endovascular intervention. In selected patients, timely debridement may be a reasonable management option, while direct angiosomal revascularization may offer additional benefits when an endovascular procedure is indicated. These findings may help clinicians refine treatment strategies and avoid unnecessary interventions without compromising limb-related outcomes.

items.title: Programmable functional RNA design with a virtual scientist.
items.abstract: Programmable functional RNA design is central to synthetic biology and therapeutics, yet both human expertise and existing computational methods struggle to directly program the three-dimensional structures that govern function. Here we introduce RhoAgent, an agentic system that designs RNA candidates and iteratively refines them using experimental feedback. RhoAgent uses RDiff, a diffusion-based generative tool conditioned on base interactions and functional motifs. First, we validate RhoAgent by generating diverse and active ribozymes with only 40-70% sequence similarity to their wild-type counterparts. Second, we enhance the cleavage efficiency of the structurally uncharacterized hovlinc ribozyme by up to sixfold relative to the human-expert-truncated construct. Furthermore, RhoAgent generates a fluorogenic aptamer scaffold that improves fluorescence by 230% relative to the wild-type aptamer. Finally, we design three-dimensional scaffolds that spatially position two distinct functional cores, creating aptamer-based Förster resonance energy transfer systems. This design overcomes a key barrier in compositional RNA design by preserving the binding activities of both components.

items.title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer: a multicentre development, validation, and testing study.

sections.objective: Peritoneal recurrence remains a common and fatal complication following curative gastric cancer surgery. Tertiary lymphoid structures are crucial indicators of immune response in cancer, and their maturation is associated with better prognosis and therapy outcomes. Evaluation of these structures could improve patient stratification for treatment of cancer but is hindered by the invasive and biased nature of histological methods. This study aimed to explore a non-invasive radiological method of assessment in patients with gastric cancer, using a novel multitask hybrid model to predict the presence and maturation status of tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence-free survival.
sections.methods: We developed CTransNet, a multitask hybrid model combining a convolutional neural network (ResNet50) and a Transformer model to predict tertiary lymphoid structure maturation and peritoneal recurrence-free survival in patients with gastric cancer. The study used retrospective data from eight Chinese cohorts of patients treated for gastric cancer at Nanfang Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, and Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (one training cohort, two internal validation cohorts, three external validation cohorts, and two independent cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 inhibitors for at least two cycles). Patients were classified into three categories based on the presence and maturation of tertiary lymphoid structures (identified using haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry staining): TLS0 (absent tertiary lymphoid structures), TLS1 (primary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures without germinal centres), and TLS2 (secondary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures with germinal centres [ie, more mature structures]). Peritoneal recurrence was assessed using imaging (ultrasonography, CT, or PET-CT), clinical signs, or reoperation. We evaluated the accuracy of the multitask hybrid model in classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Patients were stratified into risk groups using the median predicted score from the training cohort (high vs low), which was then applied to the validation cohorts. Survival outcomes (peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. We also analysed the relationships between predicted scores and responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
sections.results: Patients in the Chinese cohorts were recruited between Jan 1, 2005, and Feb 28, 2022. In the training cohort, for classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status, values for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0·910 (95% CI 0·882-0·938) for TLS0, 0·925 (0·899-0·951) for TLS1, and 0·953 (0·933-0·974) for TLS2. For predicting peritoneal recurrence-free survival, the model achieved a concordance index of 0·654 (95% CI 0·620-0·688) in the training cohort. Across all cohorts, patients with low model scores had substantially higher 5-year peritoneal recurrence rates than those with high scores (eg, 66·69%, 95% CI 60·11-73·27 vs 26·28%, 20·05-32·51; p<0·0001 in the training cohort). Multivariate analysis confirmed risk stratification based on the multitask hybrid model score as an independent predictor of peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. Analysis of patients with stage II or stage III disease in the training cohort and internal and external validation cohorts showed that in those with low predicted scores versus high predicted scores, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in patients with low scores but not those with high scores. In the immunotherapy cohorts, objective response rates were higher for patients with high predicted scores than for those with low predicted scores (54·5% vs 5·6%; p<0·0001 in immunotherapy cohort 1 and 53·1% vs 9·7%; p=0·0010 in immunotherapy cohort 2).
sections.conclusion: By accurately predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status, peritoneal recurrence, and survival, the multitask hybrid model shows strong potential as a non-invasive tool for personalised gastric cancer care. The model's potential to identify patients who might benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy and are more likely to respond to immunotherapy could help clinicians to optimise treatment strategies.

items.title: Closing the evidence gap: a life course and neurodiversity-informed participatory scoping review of healthy ageing randomised controlled trials in adults with developmental disabilities.
items.abstract: Adults aged 18 years and older with developmental disabilities experience disproportionate adverse health outcomes across the life course and shortened life expectancy. We conducted a participatory scoping review of randomised controlled trials of healthy ageing interventions for adults with developmental disabilities, informed by the WHO life course framework and neurodiversity principles. We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection on June 25, 2024, and April 10, 2025, and charted study characteristics and framework alignment. We included 79 trials with 8221 participants. Although 77 (97%) of 79 studies addressed at least one functional ability, only 25 (32%) targeted life course transitions, 28 (35%) targeted multiple ecosystem levels, 22 (28%) used participatory approaches, and 20 (25%) used strengths-based approaches. Life course and neurodiversity principles were incompletely integrated into intervention research, indicating opportunities to address developmental transitions, multiple ecosystem levels, social and community participation, and strengths across the life course.

items.title: Mortality and prognostic factors in invasive aspergillosis: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Invasive aspergillosis remains a life-threatening infection, but robust real-world mortality estimates are scarce. We aimed to generate contemporary overall and subgroup-specific mortality estimates for invasive aspergillosis using individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and IPD meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science for articles published between Jan 1, 2015, and Dec 31, 2024, that reported mortality of at least ten patients with invasive aspergillosis diagnosed using established criteria, with clearly defined and analysed follow-up periods. Corresponding authors were contacted to obtain IPD on demographics, underlying conditions, site of invasive aspergillosis, diagnostic certainty, and mortality. The primary outcome was overall all-cause mortality at 4, 6, 12, and 24 weeks, 1 year, and 2 years after invasive aspergillosis diagnosis. Secondary outcomes were intensive care unit (ICU) mortality and in-hospital mortality. One-stage IPD meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled mortality. This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025621772).
sections.results: 16 020 articles were identified, of which 9686 articles were screened after removal of duplicates. Of the articles screened, 209 studies including 15 357 patients were eligible. IPD were obtained from 46 studies, comprising 3880 patients. Across IPD cohorts, patients were predominantly middle-aged and had pulmonary involvement, and probable invasive aspergillosis was the most common diagnostic certainty; classic immunocompromised host factors were common in the mortality-after-invasive aspergillosis-diagnosis cohort, whereas COVID-19 predominated in the ICU mortality cohort. Estimated overall mortality was 26·7% (95% CI 21·0-38·2) at 4 weeks, 32·0% (26·9-42·6) at 6 weeks, 41·7% (34·9-55·1) at 12 weeks, 48·5% (41·4-61·4) at 24 weeks, 53·8% (46·8-64·0) at 1 year, and 57·2% (49·7-68·3) at 2 years. ICU mortality was 57·1% (47·5-66·5) and in-hospital mortality was 46·7% (39·4-54·1). By underlying condition, estimated 4-week mortality was highest among patients with ICU admission (42·9%, 30·4-53·2). By site, estimated 4-week mortality was 27·2% (21·3-40·0) for pulmonary, 21·1% (15·1-28·9) for sinus, and 40·4% (35·0-54·5) for brain invasive aspergillosis. The overall pooled estimates yielded I2 values of 93·2% (92·0-94·3) for 4-week mortality, 89·5% (87·6-91·2) for in-hospital mortality, and 92·3% (90·8-93·5) for ICU mortality.
sections.conclusion: Mortality among patients with invasive aspergillosis remains high despite modern diagnostic and therapeutic advances. Greater vigilance, earlier diagnosis, and timely antifungal treatment are needed, particularly for patients with newly recognised host factors, including ICU admission and COVID-19.

items.title: Population-scale identification of gut commensals that antagonize antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat, yet microbiome-encoded defenses against antibiotic resistance gene (ARG)-associated pathogens remain poorly defined. Here, we analyze 12,238 human gut metagenomes and prioritize 159 commensal species ("coexcluders") that show inverse associations with ARG-associated pathogenic taxa. These taxa carry low ARG burdens and encode candidate antimicrobial peptide repertoires. For Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, deep learning-guided mining of 2,053 genomes reveals 6,737 peptides prevalent in the human gut that inversely associate with ARG-associated pathogens. In antibiotic-perturbed mice, F. prausnitzii reduces the resistance burden and restores ecological stability, with peptide enrichment. These peptides show preferential activity against antibiotic-resistant E. coli derivatives while sparing commensals, which is consistent with a kill-the-winner dynamic. Anaerobic coculture reveals resistance-dependent peptide induction, linking the resistance phenotype to competitive suppression. This work establishes a scalable, resistance-guided framework that links population-level ecological signatures to strain-resolved microbial and molecular candidates, providing a basis for mechanistic and therapeutic development.

items.title: Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.

sections.objective: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted. This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs.
sections.methods: We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps.
sections.results: Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern.
sections.conclusion: During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

items.title: Host-microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues.
items.abstract: As a primary port of pathogen entry, the intestinal mucosa has developed a sophisticated set of defences to ward off infections. Investigating the human-specific intestinal barrier responses to pathogens is limited by the lack of models integrating the necessary architectural complexity with an autologous immune compartment1. Here we developed engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon combining a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. These tissues recapitulate morphological and functional properties that are region specific and compare with those of the native organ. We use the model to characterize the human epithelial response to Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium at the single-cell level, uncovering the distinct gene regulatory networks that underpin luminal versus intracellular pathogen presence. Invaded epithelial cells initiate an IL-18 signalling axis that triggers cytotoxic T cell activation, resulting in epithelial shedding and barrier disruption. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial and immune compartments, providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

items.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene.
items.abstract: van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1-4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7-12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain-Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands.
items.abstract: Islands account for a disproportionate share of global biodiversity1, yet insects, including invaluable pollinators such as bees2, remain underrepresented in island biogeography research3. Here we present a global checklist of island bees, recording 4,147 species across 305 islands. Although islands comprise only about 6% of the Earth's land area, they support around 20% of known global bee diversity, and 42% of insular species are endemic, making up around 8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness peaks at mid-latitudes (at least in the Northern Hemisphere), mirroring continental trends4. Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa5. The strength of island species-area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in Mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. The number of endemic species is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Major centres of bee endemism include Madagascar, Malesia (the Greater Sundas and New Guinea) and the Hawaiian islands, where a single large radiation of Hylaeus (Nesoprosopis) dominates6. Among islands that are capable of supporting endemic species, endemism scales strongly with total richness. These findings highlight the need to integrate island bee diversity into global conservation planning and position bees as a model for understanding insect evolution and conservation on islands.

items.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide.
items.abstract: Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution1-4. They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals5,6. Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes7, and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology8. Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

items.title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs.
items.abstract: Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light-matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6-arising from collective quantum interference among emitters-has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open new opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8-10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

items.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts.
items.abstract: Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics1,2. Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented2, the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria, guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei. Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial-chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

items.title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand-receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

items.title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape.
items.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies1-7. Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers1-4,8,9. Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8+ T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies10-13. However, ferroptotic cells limit this response8-10,14, resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE2 production or disrupting PGE2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8+ T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

items.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits.
items.abstract: Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing1. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses2. Exciton-polaritons, hybrid light-matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms3-5. However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry-Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

items.title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin.
items.abstract: Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell-cell contact1. These networks are among the stiffest found in the cytoskeleton and can generate large pushing stresses against stationary obstacles2-5. When grown against a controlled opposing stress in an atomic force microscope6 or inside the cell7, branched networks alter their own architecture to adapt their compressional stiffness to their environment, but the underpinnings of their mechanics and adaptability are unclear. Here we show that their high density and low connectivity place them outside the scope of standard elastic network models for actin. We show that they are instead dominated by the proliferation of interfilament contacts under compression. This places branched actin in the same category as undercoordinated fibrous materials such as sheep's wool. When the network is grown under force, filaments entangle as if knitted together and trap contacts in their structure. Trapped contacts have a similar role as crosslinkers in rigidifying the network and are thus key to its active adaptive mechanics.

items.title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity.
items.abstract: Tropical land-use intensification threatens global biodiversity, yet most assessments of tropical agricultural landscapes focus on local-scale biodiversity, overlooking how land use restructures biodiversity across space and multiple taxa. Here we provide an ecosystem-wide assessment of 24 taxonomic groups across all domains of life-encompassing 40,049 species-along a land-use intensification gradient from lowland forests to intensively managed smallholder cash-crop monocultures in Indonesian landscapes. Despite widespread losses of landscape and local multidiversity1 in monocultures (approximately 78% and 50%, respectively), we found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, monocultures exhibit a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness for aboveground taxa. Such patterns of differentiation may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization via early stages of assemblage simplification. Biotic differentiation has the potential to partly mitigate biodiversity losses by positively affecting γ-diversity. This opens management options, including the conservation of existing remnants of traditional agriculture and the implementation of sustainable management practices2-4. Our results demonstrate that tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity not only through species loss, but also via a pervasive reorganization of community composition across trophic levels. Conserving tropical biodiversity, therefore, requires a multi-taxon, landscape-scale perspective that explicitly integrates agricultural land uses with the protection of natural and semi-natural habitats to reconcile agricultural production and conservation.

items.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids.
items.abstract: Resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections1-3, and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer-Ambegaokar-McCumber-Halperin theory of phase slips4. In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model5. The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.

items.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia.
items.abstract: Hominin fossils and genetic evidence indicate that several hominin populations occupied East and Southeast Asia during the Middle and Late Pleistocene epoch1-10. Homo erectus fossils remain scarce in southern China and mainland Southeast Asia4,8,11. Here we report nine newly discovered late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves at the Chongzuo study area, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China, dated to around 324-184 thousand years ago12. Palaeoproteomics reveals the presence of an endogenous dental proteome in all five hominin teeth studied molecularly. Four teeth contain a derived H. erectus substitution in ameloblastin that to date has been observed only in older Middle Pleistocene H. erectus specimens from China13. The proteomes of these four teeth differ from the previous H. erectus proteomes from China at another ameloblastin position, suggesting that these specimens represent a previously unsampled H. erectus population. Morphometric and geometric morphometric methods support an attribution of these teeth to H. erectus, as well as four additional teeth. This fills a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of H. erectus in East Asia. The fifth tooth studied proteomically, PA1796, is morphologically distinct from H. erectus, Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis) and modern humans (Homo sapiens), and does not contain the H. erectus-derived amino acid sequence. The late survival of H. erectus on mainland East Asia suggests that at least two hominin lineages, H. erectus and Homo longi (Denisovans)6,7, possibly represented by PA1796, were present in the region towards the end of the Middle Pleistocene, with the first documented occurrence of H. sapiens not much later5.

items.title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits.
items.abstract: A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain. For example, neurons at many levels of the visual hierarchy are attuned to motion direction1-5. However, links between motion-selective computations and cell types at various stages of the visual hierarchy remain unidentified. A key first step in delineating these relationships is to map the wiring diagrams that connect different motion-selective cell types. Here we establish a systematic, cell-type-specific circuit-mapping method, combining an anterograde trans-neuronal fluorescent tracer (mWGA-mCherry)6 with spatial transcriptomics (multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH))7,8 to establish TransA-MERFISH. We used TransA-MERFISH to comprehensively map the synaptic target cell types of four retinal ganglion cell subclasses in superior colliculus (SC) at cell-type resolution. These experiments unexpectedly revealed that retinal on-off direction-selective ganglion cells (ooDSGCs) innervate several direction-selective SC cell types, but do not innervate a SC cell type that was previously reported to display strong direction-selective responses. We validated these results using orthogonal approaches and demonstrated the sensitivity and specificity of TransA-MERFISH. Functional studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that these computationally distinct, ooDSGC-dependent and -independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Together, our study establishes TransA-MERFISH as a robust framework for mapping wiring diagrams at the cell-type level and uncovers divergent computational mechanisms of motion detection in early visual processing.

items.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China.
items.abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka)2. Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil3, Sangiran4 and Ngandong2 (in Java) open woodland-grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus5, found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens, and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus.

items.title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum.
items.abstract: The genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally important group of grasses1,2. Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. Comparative analyses reveal extensive structural variation, including inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that disrupt proximal collinearity and reflect lineage-specific genome remodelling. Single-copy gene phylogenies identify ancient hybridization, segmental exchange and introgression, revealing pervasive reticulate evolution during Hordeum diversification. We uncover widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum, with many transferred genes showing evidence of transcription and functional integration. Retrotransposon proliferation explains genome size variation and provides insights into polyploid genome evolution. Whole-genome alignments reveal contrasting evolutionary dynamics: whereas coding sequences remain highly conserved, regulatory elements undergo rapid turnover, providing a rich source of regulatory diversity for phenotypic evolution. Case studies of vernalization and glume development demonstrate how natural variation in regulatory and coding sequences contributes to flowering time and floral morphology. This comprehensive pangenomic framework establishes Hordeum as a model for studying genome evolution, structural variation and the genetic basis of adaptive traits, offering new avenues for barley improvement.

items.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass.
items.abstract: Bogong moths (Agrotis infusa) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps1,2. These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds3, suggesting that their magnetic sense4 probably harnesses the Earth's magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet-blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense5.

items.title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites.
items.abstract: Twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network-a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1-3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex-antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a new and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials.

items.title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices.
items.abstract: Position information underpins many modern technologies, from navigation and timing to authentication and critical infrastructure1-3. However, classical methods of proving that information originates from a particular position are vulnerable to spoofing4-6. This limitation can be overcome with quantum technologies7-16, but current protocols rely on trust in quantum hardware that can be undermined17,18, or require quantum computers and bounds on adversarial computation19. Nevertheless, there has been considerable interest in experimental demonstrations, and aspects of these protocols have been implemented20-22. Here we introduce and experimentally demonstrate the Bell-test quantum position verification protocol for device-independent quantum position verification that guarantees security with only observed correlations from a loophole-free Bell test23-25 across a quantum network. In the experiment, we implement a version of this device-independent protocol against adversaries who, before each trial, are weakly entangled. Our demonstration achieves a one-dimensional localization 2.47(2) times smaller than the best, necessarily non-remote, classical localization protocol. Compared with classical protocols with identical latencies, the localization volume is 4.53(5) times smaller, representing a certifiable quantum advantage. The general Bell-test protocol is loss-tolerant and secure against adversaries with substantial quantum resources. This work allows digital security to be anchored to physically trusted locations, enabling new position-based authentication protocols for applications such as financial transactions, legal agreements and securing critical infrastructure26-29.

items.title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi.
items.abstract: One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p-wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1-3). Achieving p-wave superconductivity4 and its magnetic analogue5-characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p-wave spin-polarized Fermi surface-remains a grand challenge6,7. Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p-wave magnets5,7-10, spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p-wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves Sy polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted Sy exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p-wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics10, topological matter7, superconductivity11 and beyond.

items.title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species.
items.abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1. Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope2,3. Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

items.title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies.
items.abstract: The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate-forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

items.title: Physical activity coaching and text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK): hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of a physical activity coaching intervention compared with text messaging intervention and waitlist control in adults with mobility limitations.
sections.methods: Three arm, pragmatic, superiority, hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial. 512 community dwelling adults (≥18 years) who self-reported mobility limitations (difficulty or inability to walk 800 m, with or without a walking aid) but were still able to leave home without physical assistance from another person. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to: a six month, multicomponent intervention including fortnightly physiotherapist delivered telephone coaching (coaching group, n=172); a six month, multicomponent intervention including regular unidirectional text messages (texting group, n=171); and no intervention for six months, followed by the six month text messaging intervention (waitlist control group, n=169). Participants and physiotherapists were unmasked to group allocation.
sections.results: Participants' mean age was 69 years (standard deviation (SD) 10 years) and 76% (n=388/511) were women. More than half (n=263/508, 51%) of participants reported multiple long term conditions as the main reason for their mobility limitation. At six months, mean daily steps were 931 higher (95% confidence interval 409 to 1452 steps; P=0.001) in the coaching group (mean 7256 (SD 3736) steps) compared with waitlist group (6526 (3003) steps); and 571 steps higher (58 to 1084, P=0.03) compared with the texting group (6529 (3029) steps). Mean daily steps in the texting group were 359 higher (-91 to 810, P=0.12) compared with the waitlist group, but this was not statistically significant. The number of adverse events was similar between groups (11/172 (6%) in the coaching group, 7/171 (4%) in the texting group, and 13/169 (8%) in the waitlist group) and none were serious.
sections.conclusion: A person centred coaching intervention produced modest increases in physical activity and was more effective than a less intensive texting intervention or no intervention among adults with mobility limitations.
sections.other: Health services and general communities across five Australian states, 19 December 2018 to 7 March 2023. The primary outcome was device measured mean daily steps at six months, analysed according to treatment allocation using all available data. Outcome assessors and data analysts were masked to group allocation.

items.title: Effect of intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide and sodium bicarbonate on spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women after induction of labour (SAINT): multicentre randomised placebo controlled factorial trial.

sections.objective: To determine whether intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, and their combination increase the rate of spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women undergoing induction of labour.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 2×2 factorial phase 3 trial (SAINT). Nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with a singleton live fetus in cephalic presentation at term with an indication for induction of labour. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to oral sodium bicarbonate (4×1 g per dose) plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide (20 mg per dose), oral sodium bicarbonate plus intravenous placebo, oral placebo plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide, or double placebo. The investigational medicinal product was administered at the onset of active labour and repeated every four hours to a maximum of three doses.
sections.results: Between 4 January 2023 and 29 January 2025, 3094 nulliparous women were randomised, and 2963 comprised the full analysis set. Spontaneous vaginal birth occurred in 57% (422/741) in the bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide arm, 61% (445/734) in the bicarbonate arm, 61% (449/741) in the hyoscine butylbromide arm, and 56% (422/747) in the double placebo arm. Marginal risk differences for spontaneous vaginal birth compared with double placebo were -0.2 (95% confidence interval -5.1 to 4.7; P=0.93) percentage points for combined treatment, 3.1 (-1.7 to 8.0; P=0.21) percentage points for bicarbonate, and 4.0 (-0.8 to 8.9; P=0.10) percentage points for hyoscine butylbromide. Serious adverse events were similar between groups, and no treatment related serious morbidity or deaths were observed.
sections.conclusion: No clear evidence was found that intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, or their combination increased spontaneous vaginal birth compared with placebo. Although small beneficial effects cannot be excluded, the findings do not support routine intrapartum use of either agent to facilitate spontaneous vaginal birth after induction of labour.
sections.other: 11 Norwegian hospitals providing comprehensive obstetric care. Spontaneous vaginal birth (no instrumental or caesarean delivery).

items.title: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems.
items.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite-silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

items.title: Outcomes of cataract surgery in eyes with vitreomacular traction: a retrospective cohort study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the anatomical and visual outcomes after uncomplicated phacoemulsification in eyes with vitreomacular traction (VMT).
sections.methods: This retrospective observational cohort study included consecutive patients with VMT undergoing cataract surgery. Clinical records and optical coherence tomography (OCT) images were reviewed for corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), axial length, central subfield thickness (CST), VMT configuration and width, intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), cotton ball sign, postoperative cystoid macular oedema (CMO), VMT release, macular hole formation and subsequent vitrectomy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with VMT-release.
sections.results: Two hundred and two eyes of 202 patients were included (mean age, 77.1 ± 6.7 years; mean follow-up, 7.3 ± 5.7 months). Postoperative CDVA improved to 0.15 ± 0.16 LogMAR (P < 0.01). CMO developed in 42 eyes (20.8%) and occurred in 15 of 95 eyes receiving ketorolac (15.8%) and 27 of 107 eyes not receiving ketorolac (25.2%, χ² = 2.73, P = 0.099; OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.28-1.12). VMT-release occurred in 14 eyes (6.9%) and macular hole occurred in 6 eyes (3.0%). The presence of IRF, SRF, or cotton ball sign was associated with VMT-release (χ² = 6.83, P = 0.009), whereas age, AL, CST, VMT-morphology and VMT-width were not. Six eyes (3.0%) required secondary vitrectomy.
sections.conclusion: Standalone cataract surgery was associated with improved CDVA and low rates of postoperative macular hole formation and secondary vitrectomy in eyes with VMT. However, postoperative CMO was common, occurring in approximately one-fifth of eyes.

items.title: Incidence and visual outcomes of post-intravitreal injection endophthalmitis: a single-centre analysis of 224,397 injections.

sections.objective: Post-injection endophthalmitis (PIE) is a rare, vision-threatening complication of intravitreal injections (IVIs). As IVI volumes rise globally, optimising prevention and management is crucial. This study evaluated PIE incidence, risk factors, microbiology, and outcomes over ten years.
sections.methods: A retrospective cohort study of 224,397 IVIs. We analysed demographics, agent type, and preparation (pre-filled syringe [PFS] vs. manual aliquoting).
sections.results: Overall endophthalmitis incidence was 0.029% (n = 65), and 0.026% for anti-VEGFs. PFS-ranibizumab had the lowest incidence (0.014%) and was significantly safer than manually prepared bevacizumab (0.039%; OR: 2.74 [95% CI: 1.36-5.55], p = 0.003); vial-sourced aflibercept (0.027%) was intermediate and not statistically distinguishable from either. Culture positivity was 33.8% (n = 22), predominantly Gram-positive (81.8%), with Staphylococcus epidermidis being the most common (45.5%). In univariate analysis, culture positivity was the sole predictor of worse final visual acuity (VA) (p = 0.030), though limited by small sample sizes. Median VA worsened from 0.61 logMAR at baseline to 2.10 logMAR at presentation, recovering to 1.80 logMAR at final visit (p 0.05).
sections.conclusion: Dexamethasone implants, with their larger applicator, carried the highest risk. Among anti-VEGFs, PFS ranibizumab demonstrated the most favourable safety profile, with the lowest incidence of PIE. Manual immediate-use bevacizumab aliquoting is a safe, cost-effective alternative in resource-limited settings. In univariate analysis, culture positivity emerged as a negative prognostic factor, though this finding is limited by small sample sizes. Given unpredictable TAI responses, aggressive monitoring and a low PPV threshold are essential.

items.title: Comprehensive evaluation of drug-related vision disorder risk in breast cancer patients: a global pharmacovigilance analysis.

sections.objective: Breast cancer, the most common malignancy in women worldwide, has a high incidence and mortality rate, with treatments like chemotherapy and targeted therapies improving survival but causing ocular toxicity.
sections.methods: In this study, we analysed potential risk signals for vision disorders in breast cancer patients using the FAERS from January 2020 to December 2024. Disproportionate analysis was performed to identify positive signals, with a reporting odds ratio (ROR). Multiplicative models were used to assess drug-drug interactions. Moreover, the time to onset of vision disorders was also evaluated.
sections.results: A total of 2402 cases of vision disorders occurring in breast cancer patients were included. The median onset time for vision disorders was 17.5 days (IQR: 2.5-84.5), with hospitalisation (19.9%) and disability (7.4%) as common outcomes. Among the top 20 most frequently used drugs, tamoxifen (ROR = 2.29, 95% CI: 1.68-3.13) and trastuzumab emtansine (ROR = 1.98, 95% CI: 1.49-2.64) showed the strongest associations with vision disorders. Combination therapy analysis identified positive interaction signals for ribociclib with most endocrine therapies.
sections.conclusion: This study systematically evaluated potential risk signals for vision disorders associated with medication use in breast cancer patients. These findings may support clinical vigilance for potential ocular AEs but do not quantify treatment risk or establish causality.

items.title: Coffee saucer grading system: a novel method for stratifying corneal trauma in the International Globe and Adnexal Trauma Epidemiology Study (IGATES) registry.

sections.objective: Ophthalmic trauma represents a leading cause of monocular blindness. Corneal injuries constitute a substantial subset of open globe injuries (OGIs), yet existing classifications insufficiently capture their anatomical heterogeneity. This study evaluated the prognostic utility of the Coffee Saucer Grading (CSG) system for stratifying corneal trauma and distinguishing subzone-specific visual outcomes and complications.
sections.results: Among 3577 patients, 81.0% (n = 2897) were male, and the mean age was 31.6 years (SD 19.4). Zone 1A injuries were most common at 36.8% (n = 881), followed by Zone 1D at 25.0% (n = 599), Zone 1B at 23.0% (n = 550), and Zone 1C at 15.1% (n = 362). Mean initial and final CDVA were 1.6 and 1.2 LogMAR, respectively (p < 0.001). Visual outcomes, odds of blindness, and complication profiles varied by subzone (p < 0.001). Compared with Zone 1B, the odds of blindness were higher for Zone 1A (OR 1.68), 1C (OR 1.87), and 1D (OR 3.30) injuries (p < 0.001). Zone 1D injuries demonstrated the highest complication burden (p = 0.003).
sections.conclusion: The CSG system identified distinct subzone-specific differences in visual outcomes and complications, demonstrating the prognostic relevance of corneal wound topography. This reproducible framework may facilitate standardised trauma phenotyping, risk stratification, and multicentre research.
sections.other: This retrospective study analysed corneal OGIs across 12 countries within the International Globe and Adnexal Trauma Epidemiology Study (IGATES) registry. Corneal OGIs were categorised into 4 CSG subzones: Zone 1A (central cornea), Zone 1B (paracentral cornea), Zone 1 C (limbal region), and Zone 1D (combined corneal-limbal involvement). Corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), blindness (CDVA < 6/60), and ocular complications were compared across subzones.

items.title: Clinical characteristics associated with elevated serum adiponectin in patients with lower extremity artery disease.

sections.objective: Elevated circulating adiponectin has been associated with poor prognosis in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD). However, the clinical characteristics underlying elevated adiponectin in patients with LEAD remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify the clinical and computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition characteristics associated with elevated serum adiponectin and to evaluate the association between serum adiponectin and 2-year overall survival in patients with LEAD.
sections.methods: This prospective observational study included 80 patients with LEAD who underwent lower extremity revascularization between May 2021 and December 2023. Serum adiponectin levels were measured at the time of revascularization. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, and CT-derived body composition parameters were compared between patients with high and low serum adiponectin levels, classified according to the median value. 2-year overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. The association between serum adiponectin and 2-year mortality was also evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression adjusted for age. Factors associated with serum adiponectin were assessed using univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses.
sections.results: Among the 80 patients, 40 were classified into the high adiponectin group and 40 into the low adiponectin group. Patients with high adiponectin were significantly older and had lower body mass index (BMI), visceral fat area (VFA), subcutaneous fat area (SFA), and triglyceride levels than those with low adiponectin. 2-year overall survival was significantly lower in the high adiponectin group than in the low adiponectin group (78.6% vs 94.8%, p = .0330). After adjustment for age, high serum adiponectin remained significantly associated with 2-year mortality (HR = 2.22, 95% CI, 1.08 to 5.83, p = .0278). In multivariable linear regression analysis, VFA remained independently and inversely associated with serum adiponectin after adjustment for age, BMI, skeletal muscle area, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (β = -0.0126 per 10 cm2 increase, 95% CI, -0.0221 to -0.0032, p = .0096).
sections.conclusion: Elevated serum adiponectin was associated with poor 2-year survival in patients with LEAD. Reduced CT-derived VFA was independently associated with elevated serum adiponectin even after adjustment for BMI and other clinical factors. These findings suggest that elevated adiponectin may characterize a LEAD phenotype with reduced visceral adiposity and adverse prognosis.

items.title: Virotherapy: Viral Vectors for Skin Cancers, Vaccines, and Gene Therapy.

sections.objective: Viral vectors therapies have entered clinical dermatology through approved treatments for advanced melanoma and dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB). However, many dermatologists remain unfamiliar with patient selection, referral pathways, and the expanding role of these therapies in cutaneous disease. To provide a practical review of currently available and emerging viral vector therapies relevant to dermatologic practice.
sections.methods: This paper includes a narrative review of clinical trials, regulatory approvals, and emerging evidence involving oncolytic virotherapy, topical gene therapy, and selected vaccine-based immune modulation strategies.
sections.results: Oncolytic herpes simplex virus (HSV)-based therapies have demonstrated meaningful clinical activity in advanced melanoma, including patients with disease progression after immune checkpoint inhibition. Emerging data and trials suggest benefit in selected nonmelanoma skin cancers. In DEB, topical beremagene geperpavec-svdt (B-VEC) has established viral vector-mediated gene therapy as an effective treatment capable of promoting durable wound closure and improving quality of life. Additional applications, including vaccine-mediated immune modulation and in vivo cellular therapies, remain investigational.
sections.conclusion: Viral vector therapeutics are becoming increasingly relevant to dermatology. Familiarity with currently approved therapies, appropriate referral candidates, and evolving clinical applications will help dermatologists integrate these advances into patient care.
sections.other: Many emerging applications are supported right now by only early-phase clinical or preclinical studies.

items.title: Proteome- and phenome-wide studies identify circulating protein drivers of kidney diseases.

sections.objective: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (PWMR) provides a genetic framework to identify circulating proteins causally implicated in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and prioritize them for drug discovery. However, the diverse etiologies of CKD and clinical presentations make it difficult to translate proteomic findings into actionable targets. Here, we studied protein associations with longitudinal kidney outcomes, CKD subtypes, and phenome-wide traits to identify proteins that are causally relevant and pharmacologically actionable.
sections.methods: We performed a PWMR study using cis-pQTLs as genetic instruments for 2807 circulating proteins from four proteogenomic cohorts (ARIC, Fenland, deCODE, and UK Biobank) and tested their effects across four kidney outcomes (eGFR, incident CKD, incident kidney failure, annualized eGFR slope) in up to 464,631 of Million Veteran Program participants. Proteins meeting proteome-wide significance underwent sensitivity testing, Bayesian colocalization, and external replication in CKDGen Consortium information. The same instruments were re-tested against nine diagnosis code-defined CKD subtypes using genome wide association studies meta-analysis across the Million Veteran Program participants, UK Biobank, and FinnGen, and against 1020 phecodes to distinguish kidney-restricted from systemic effects. Druggability was evaluated using ChEMBL annotations layered onto high-confidence STRING protein-protein interaction networks.
sections.results: We identified 93 proteins with proteome-wide significance, and twelve remained robust across sensitivity testing (ANGPTL3, FAM213A, GCKR, GSTA1, IDI2, INHBA, INHBC, MANBA, MICB, MST1, NRG4, UMOD). Forty-seven proteins mapped to at least one of nine kidney disease subtypes, with distinct patterns across diabetic, hypertensive, and glomerular kidney diseases. Phenome-wide testing separated seven proteins with kidney-restricted associations from those with broader systemic effects. Thirty-four proteins were pharmacologic targets, nominating candidates such as IL-1 pathway blockade for diabetic kidney disease and ANGPTL3 inhibition for podocyte protection.
sections.conclusion: Our integrative PWMR framework resolves circulating protein targets across CKD etiologies, separates kidney-restricted from systemic effects, and delivers actionable targets that may accelerate therapeutic innovation for CKD. About one-third of the 93 proteins could be targeted with existing or investigational medications.

items.title: Characterization of the Urine Proteome Using the Olink Explore 3072 Platform.

sections.objective: Urinary proteins are valuable biomarkers for physiological processes and early detection/monitoring of kidney diseases. However, comprehensive quantification and characterization of the urine proteome using a high-throughput platform remains limited.
sections.methods: Using the affinity-based Olink Explore 3072 proteomics assay, we quantified 2868 proteins in urine samples from 1268 participants of the German Chronic Kidney Disease (GCKD) study.
sections.results: Protein detectability in urine, defined as the percentage of samples with measurements above the limit of detection, showed a bimodal distribution: 659 (23%) proteins had high (over 80%) and 1336 proteins (47%) had low (under 20%) detectability, with stable detectability across strata of albuminuria and kidney function. More than 95% of highly detectable proteins had previously been identified in urine by mass spectrometry. Highly detectable proteins were enriched for extracellular, exosomal, and cell surface localization, and for expression in hepatocytes, immune cells and kidney proximal tubule cells. Comparison with plasma detectability from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project identified proteins of likely kidney origin, including LRP2 (megalin) and NPHS2 (podocin). In a multivariable adjusted model of 13 clinical variables, albuminuria and an individual's sex showed significant associations with 779 and 670 proteins, respectively. Specific chronic kidney disease etiologies showed associations with 105 proteins, although etiology explained only a small proportion of protein variance. Correlation analysis revealed biologically meaningful protein clusters reflecting shared cellular compartments, tissue of origin, and molecular interactions.
sections.conclusion: Large-scale urine proteomic profiling using a high-multiplex affinity-based platform captures biologically meaningful molecular variation associated with clinical variables and chronic kidney disease, providing a valuable resource for biomarker discovery and future targeted studies.

items.title: Comparative Early Outcomes of Total Transfemoral vs. Upper Extremity Access for Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) Implantation.

sections.objective: Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.
