sections.methods: A retrospective review of consecutive patients undergoing TAMBE implantation at a single centre between April 2020 and January 2026 was performed. Patients were stratified by access strategy into TFA and UEA. The primary outcomes were thirty day mortality and major adverse events (MAEs).
sections.results: One hundred patients underwent TAMBE implantation during the study period, of whom 32 underwent TFA and 68 UEA. The majority of aneurysms treated were thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (61%), and 45% of patients had a prior endovascular intervention with no significant difference between groups (all p > .050). Mean operative time (232.8 ± 92.4 minutes vs. 250.8 ± 77.3 minutes; p = .18) and fluoroscopy time (59.2 ± 28.4 minutes vs. 48.3 ± 21.6 minutes; p = .066) were not statistically different between groups. Technical success was 91% in the TFA group compared with 99% in the UEA group (p = .095). Thirty day mortality (3% vs. 3%; p = 1.0) and MAEs (16% vs. 13%; p = .76) were not statistically different between TFA and UEA groups. Spinal cord ischaemia rates were 16% for the TFA group and 7% for the UEA group (p = .16), with most cases mild and resolved by discharge (80%). No stroke events occurred in either group. At 6 months, overall branch patency was 92% (78 of 85 branches from 22 patients), including 83% (15 of 18 branches from five patients) in the TFA group and 94% (63 of 67 branches from 17 patients) in the UEA group (p = .16).
sections.conclusion: In this single centre experience, total transfemoral TAMBE implantation was performed in selected patients, and no statistically significant differences were detected in thirty day mortality, MAEs, and technical success between access strategies. Larger studies are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist.

items.title: Revascularisation Outcomes in Symptomatic Elderly Nonagenarians with Peripheral Arterial Disease: The ROSEPAD International Registry.

sections.objective: Data regarding the outcomes of revascularisation for symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD) in nonagenarians are scarce, limited by short follow up periods and confounded by the competing risk of death. This multicentre, retrospective analysis of nonagenarians who underwent invasive treatment for symptomatic PAD (Rutherford category 3 - 6) between December 2017 and December 2023 aimed to analyse the safety and efficacy, as well as short term and medium term revascularisation outcomes in selected nonagenarians with lower limb PAD.
sections.methods: The primary endpoint was amputation free survival (AFS). Overall survival (OS), amputation free time, and freedom from any re-intervention of the index limb were additionally analysed. The cumulative incidence of major amputation and re-intervention were also estimated, accounting for the competing risk of death.
sections.results: A total of 566 patients were included. The majority underwent endovascular (81.6%), followed by open (10.6%), and hybrid revascularisation (7.8%). At 36 months, AFS was 21.4%, freedom from amputation was 85.7%, OS was 23.7%, and freedom from re-intervention was 73.7%. Men and history of coronary artery disease were associated with reduced AFS (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06 - 1.76; and hazard ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.2 - 1.99, respectively). Accounting for the competing risk of death, the cumulative incidence of major amputation was 7.3% (95% CI 5 - 9.7), 7.6% (95% CI 5.2 - 10), and 9.2% (95% CI 6.4 - 12), while the cumulative incidence of re-intervention was 14.6% (95% CI 11.4 - 17.9), 16.2% (95% CI 12.8 - 19.6), and 17.3% (95% CI 13.7 - 20.9), after 12, 24, and 36 months of follow up, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Lower limb revascularisation in selected nonagenarians with PAD was associated with a low cumulative incidence of major amputation and re-intervention. However, a high overall mortality was observed after three years of follow up.

items.title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk prediction in individuals with and without impaired spirometry.

sections.objective: Cardiovascular disease risk scores likely underestimate risk in individuals with impaired spirometry (airflow obstruction and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)).
sections.methods: Ten-year incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) ie., myocardial infarction, stroke or death from coronary heart disease, from 7 US population-based cohorts was used for this analysis. The pooled cohorts' equations' (PCE) ability to predict MACE was compared between normal and impaired spirometry. Cox-models adding spirometry, dyspnea to PCE variables were evaluated for improvement in MACE prediction.
sections.results: Among 26523 participants, those with impaired (N=7547) compared with normal (N=18932) spirometry had a higher incidence of MACE (14% vs 7%), hazard ratio 95%CI 1.25[1.17,1.34] adjusted for PCE variables. Discrimination using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)95%CI of the PCE for MACE was 0.792[0.780,0.803] vs 0.740[0.724,0.755] in normal vs impaired spirometry. Discrimination of MACE improved slightly by adding to the PCE: dyspnea plus 1)impaired spirometry 0.792[0.783,0.800], 2)PRISm, mild, moderate+ airflow obstruction 0.792[0.783,0.801], 3)FEV1%predicted, FEV1/FVC splines 0.793[0.784,0.802], compared with PCE variables 0.790[0.781,0.798]. The differences in AUC[95%CI] were: 1)0.002[0.001,0.003]p=0.002, 2)0.002[0.001,0.004]p=0.002, 3)0.003[0.002,0.005]p=0.0005 respectively. Among participants with impaired spirometry, only the model that added FEV1%predicted, FEV1/FVC continuous and dyspnea to the PCE showed improvement in AUC[95%CI], 0.750[0.735,0.765] vs 0.746[0.730,0.761] for PCE variables, difference of 0.004[0.001,0.008]p=0.008. There were no differences among models in calibration, sensitivity, specificity, overall performance, and after bootstrapping 1000 samples.
sections.conclusion: Performance of the PCE was better among individuals with normal vs impaired spirometry, despite the latter having an excess burden of MACE. Adding spirometry and dyspnea to PCE variables showed a small statistically significant improvement in MACE prediction, which may not be meaningful clinically, so other risk factors should be considered.
sections.other: How do risk scores perform between individuals with impaired and normal spirometry, and can they be improved by adding spirometry and dyspnea?

items.title: Angiopoietin-2 in Retinal Vascular Fibrosis: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications for Diabetic Retinopathy.
items.abstract: Retinal vascular fibrosis is a pathological hallmark of advanced diabetic retinopathy (DR), marking the transition from reversible vascular dysfunction to irreversible structural damage. Emerging evidence has established angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) as a crucial initiating factor in retinal vascular fibrosis. In the diabetic retina, Ang-2 expression is persistently upregulated by hyperglycemia, hypoxia, and inflammation. Through dysregulating Ang-2/Tie signaling, Ang-2 disrupts endothelial junctional proteins, promotes vascular leakage and inflammation, and induces pericyte loss, collectively leading to endothelial destabilization and microvascular abnormalities. A key mechanism underlying this fibrotic shift is endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), which drives extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation and vascular fibrosis. Ang-2 drives EndMT primarily by inducing transforming growth factor-β(TGF-β) expression. Concurrently, within a chronic inflammatory microenvironment, M2-polarized macrophages secrete numerous pro-fibrotic mediators. In addition, upregulation of tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases suppresses ECM degradation. From a therapeutic perspective, the Ang-2/Tie2 signaling has emerged as a pivotal regulatory node in vascular homeostasis and inflammatory modulation. Dual Ang-2/vascular endothelial growth factor inhibition with agents like faricimab has proven effective not only in reducing vascular leakage and neovascularization but also in curbing inflammation and halting fibrosis progression. Emerging Ang-2-targeted strategies, including long-acting fusion proteins, gene therapies, and nanoparticle-based delivery systems, aim to achieve sustained vascular stabilization and durable disease modification. We synthesize current insights into the pathogenic role of Ang-2 in DR, with a focus on its contribution to retinal vascular fibrosis and highlight recent advances in Ang-2-directed therapies. Collectively, these insights provide novel perspectives for the development of anti-retinal vascular fibrosis therapies.

items.title: Trends and Variation in Uveal Melanoma Management in the National Cancer Database, 2004-2023.
items.abstract: We evaluated presentation and management of uveal melanoma in the National Cancer Database (NCDB) from 2004-2023 with multivariable logistic regression. Enucleations decreased and globe-sparing radiation increased. Significant socioeconomic and geographic variation in treatment persisted.

items.title: Retinopathy of prematurity: causes, treatment and prevention.
items.abstract: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is initiated at preterm birth. Vascular growth in the immature retina, conditioned to low intrauterine oxygen levels, is disrupted by rapid increases in oxygen which suppress oxygen-regulated growth factors. Maternally sourced essential lipids (ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids) and insulin-like growth factor-1 are also lost. Later, maturing (but avascular) retina becomes hypoxic and nutrient starved, driving a growth factor surge often causing destructive neovascularization. Current treatments address late-stage neovascular ROP by suppressing elevated vascular endothelial growth factor levels. Recent clinical studies address the initiating events, lack of specific maternally sourced lipids and growth factors, hyperoxia-induced metabolic changes, which induce suppression of normal retinal vascularization and retinal neural maturation. Early enteral supplementation with ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids reduces risk of neovascularization. Timed topical corticosteroids during early ROP which alter metabolism to promote normal vessel growth, show great promise in preventing severe disease. Risk algorithms with near 100% sensitivity and high specificity can reduce the number of screening examinations. AI-augmented photography and ultrawide field optical coherence tomography may further refine prediction, diagnosis and treatment. This review synthesizes recent clinical paradigm shifts toward early disease prevention, highlighting how novel metabolic, pharmacological, and digital health strategies can prevent ROP-related vision loss.

items.title: Developing Static Perimetry Thresholds to Assess Visual Field Loss Severity in Patients with Retinitis Pigmentosa.

sections.objective: To assess the correlation between kinetic and static perimetry measurements in patients with retinitis pigmentosa and to develop thresholds that translate 1) mean retinal sensitivity (MRS) from static perimetry and 2) Visual field (VF) area from kinetic perimetry, into kinetic perimetry-derived VF diameter using the International Council of Ophthalmology (ICO) Visual Standards classification of vision loss severity.
sections.methods: Retrospective cross-sectional study.
sections.results: Among the 100 patients, median age was 48.5 years, disease onset at median 28 years, 52% male, 16% with XLRP. MRS correlated strongly with kinetic VF diameter (Spearman's rho 0.83) and with kinetic VF area (rho 0.81); diameter and area were correlated at rho 0.94. ROC analysis derived MRS (dB) cut-offs for vision loss severity were: ≥7.4=mild, 5.3- <7.4=moderate, 3.2- <5.3=severe, 0.6- <3.2=profound, and <0.6=near-blindness/blindness (weighted Kappa coefficient 0.59). Optimal VF area (deg2) cutoffs for distinguishing severity levels were ≥5706=mild impairment, 410 - <5706=moderate, 688- <4100= severe, 71 -<688=profound, <71=near-blindness/blindness (weighted Kappa coefficient 0.73).
sections.conclusion: Strong correlations between MRS and VF diameter measures support the feasibility of mapping static perimetry to kinetic VF diameter ICO standard to classify vision loss severity. This study addresses a critical gap in interpreting retinitis pigmentosa research findings in visual field loss assessment.
sections.other: Data were obtained from charts of 100 adults with retinitis pigmentosa who had undergone full-field static and kinetic perimetry within a 30-day interval during routine practice at Casey Eye Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, US. Full-field static and kinetic perimetry using the Octopus 900 perimetry device. Static perimetry full MRS and kinetic perimetry VF area cut-off values were derived from Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis by mapping the ICO kinetic perimetry VF diameter cut-offs to classify patients into vision loss severity groups. Youden Index and Area Under the Curve were used to determine optimal cutoff values that maximized diagnostic performance. Weighted Kappa statistics assessed the level of agreement between the derived severity classifications, and the ICO VF diameter classification standards.

items.title: Designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine for enhanced solid tumour penetration and therapy.
items.abstract: While nanomedicines hold great promise for solid tumour therapy, their penetration and access to tumour cells is limited by large glycosylated proteins called mucins that are enriched in the tumour microenvironment. Here we show that mucins induce the disassembly of self-assembled mPEG-polyester micellar nanoparticles into smaller unimers. Leveraging this finding, we designed a mucin-responsive, paclitaxel-conjugated nanomedicine (mrPNM) whose unimers are capable of escaping the mucin-binding barrier. Following intravenous injection, this designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine exhibited markedly deeper penetration than the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and albumin, resulting in 3.9- and 1.5-fold increases in tumour cell delivery, respectively, in a pancreatic mouse tumour model. The mrPNMs also achieved superior tumour growth inhibition compared to both the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and Abraxane, the FDA-approved nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel, in three solid tumour models. The mucin-responsive nanomedicine platform could provide a general strategy for improving the treatment of solid tumours.

items.title: Neotenic expansion of adult-born dentate granule cells reconfigures GABAergic inhibition to enhance social memory consolidation.
items.abstract: Immature adult-born dentate granule cells (abDGCs) show heightened synaptic and structural plasticity and preferentially contribute to hippocampal-dependent memory. Protracted maturation (neoteny) of abDGCs in higher mammals is posited to offset the decline in adult hippocampal neurogenesis by supporting increased plasticity. Here we found that selective, synchronous expansion of 4-week-old immature, but not 8-week-old mature, mouse abDGCs promotes recruitment of fast-spiking parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory interneurons (INs) in hippocampal CA3 and CA2, increases feed-forward inhibition, decreases social memory interference and enhances social memory consolidation. In vivo local field potential recordings in dorsal CA1 and CA2 revealed increased baseline power, amplitude and duration of sharp-wave ripples, as well as enhanced rate modulation by social experience. Inhibitory neuron-targeted chemogenetic manipulations implicate dorsal CA3 and CA2 INs, including parvalbumin-expressing INs, as necessary and sufficient for social memory consolidation following and sans neotenic expansion of abDGCs, respectively. Our findings suggest that neoteny of abDGCs supports cognition by increasing feed-forward inhibition in DG-CA3 and DG-CA2 and promoting network oscillations that underlie memory consolidation.

items.title: Heat-related mortality attributable to human-induced climate change: findings from the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort.

sections.objective: Over recent decades, the fact that global population health is directly and indirectly influenced by climate change has become increasingly clear, although few studies have directly attributed deaths to anthropogenic climate forcing. The impact of extreme heat is a key health risk in Brazil and is known to vary among population groups, including by age, socioeconomic condition, ethnicity, and other factors. In this Article, we aimed to quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on heat-related mortality in vulnerable populations in Brazil from 2000 to 2018.
sections.methods: We used the 100 Million (100M) Brazilian Cohort to quantify the attributable number of heat-related deaths to human-induced climate change. By 2018, the 100M Cohort assembled approximately 132 million low-income individuals in Brazil. We applied relative risk estimates generated with a distributed lag nonlinear model to modelled surface temperatures from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project climate model ensemble. The number of heat-related deaths is quantified in each immediate geographical region under factual and counterfactual (without anthropogenic forcing) scenarios. We also applied the same strategy used on the Cohort to the whole population of Brazil, using data from the Brazilian Mortality Information System, to give an independent estimate of heat-related deaths attributable to climate change in Brazil.
sections.results: We can attribute 0·89°C (90% CI 0·62-1·16) of heating in Brazil throughout 2000-18, relative to a 1961-90 baseline, to human-induced climate change. The nationwide percentage of heat-related deaths attributable to climate change in the 100M Cohort was estimated to be 51·1% (95% CI 34·8-74·9), meaning that around 75 800 heat-related deaths (95% CI 20 151-170 529) occurred in the 100M Cohort, equivalent to 2·2% (95% CI 0·6-4·9) of total non-accidental deaths. We found that extreme heat exposure causes a greater proportion of climate-attributable heat deaths than moderate heat exposure in most of Brazil's immediate geographical regions. Lastly, using the same parameters applied for the 100M Cohort, 43·7% (95% CI 27·6-71·1) of heat-related deaths in the whole Brazilian population are estimated to be attributable to climate change, broadly consistent with the Cohort-based estimate.
sections.conclusion: The results show that large numbers of heat-related deaths in Brazil would not have occurred without human influence on the climate system. The findings from the 100M Cohort were corroborated by results from a similar analysis conducted in the general population. This work highlights the urgent need to implement heat-adaptation policies to protect the Brazilian population, particularly the most vulnerable groups, and the need for ambitious global action on climate change mitigation.

items.title: Progress towards the elimination of transmission of Trypanosoma brucei gambiense in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a 25-year spatiotemporal analysis of national surveillance data.

sections.objective: Gambiense human African trypanosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease caused by the parasite Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. Multiple epidemics over more than two centuries have started in known risk areas termed human African trypanosomiasis foci, with DR Congo having historically carried the highest burden of disease. Since the latest resurgence of the disease in the 1990s, annual case notifications have decreased by 98%. In view of the WHO target to eliminate T b gambiense transmission globally by 2030, we aimed to outline areas of DR Congo that require intervention, aimed either at the elimination of ongoing transmission or at post-elimination surveillance.
sections.methods: We conducted a spatiotemporal analysis of national surveillance data on gambiense human African trypanosomiasis from across DR Congo. Screening and diagnosis data from TrypElim and the WHO Atlas of human African trypanosomiasis, geolocated at the village level and covering the period from Jan 1, 2000, to Dec 31, 2024, were combined with population data from LandScan. We then used WHO methods to outline areas at low or greater risk (≥1 case per 100 000 population) and at moderate or greater risk (≥1 case per 10 000 population) of gambiense human African trypanosomiasis for the periods 2000-04, 2005-09, 2010-14, 2015-19, and 2020-24. We assessed trends in surface area at risk over the whole study period, combining these results with infection rate data to define human African trypanosomiasis foci and estimate populations recommended to be kept under post-elimination surveillance.
sections.results: We included data on 137 690 cases of gambiense human African trypanosomiasis identified in 12 090 unique locations. Marked decreases in the areas at risk were observed over the time period studied: the area at low or greater risk decreased from 586 508 km2 (bootstrap SE 5028) at its peak in 2005-09 to 185 216 km2 (4550) in 2020-24, a 67% reduction, and the area at moderate or greater risk decreased from 340 730 km2 (2409) in 2002-06 to 8406 km2 (1385) in 2020-24, a 97% reduction. We identified 15 distinct human African trypanosomiasis foci, three of which accounted for more than 80% (99 625 of 124 467) of reported cases. At the national level, we observed a substantial decrease in infection rate among people screened in active screening campaigns, from more than 60 cases per 10 000 population in 2000 to less than one case per 10 000 population in 2024, divided into three distinct periods: a steep decline in infection rate between 2000 and 2004 (average of 29·9% per year [95% CI 25·3 to 34·3]), no significant change between 2005 and 2010 (+1·4% [-5·0 to 8·2]), and a further decrease between 2011 and 2024 (23·5% [18·9 to 27·9]), with considerable variation at a subnational level across the 15 foci.
sections.conclusion: The gambiense human African trypanosomiasis epidemic in DR Congo is now concentrated within a few foci, and elimination of transmission appears to be within reach. In foci with active transmission, sustained interventions remain imperative. New approaches, such as the presumptive treatment of individuals with suspected infection, could pave the way to the elimination of transmission, after which post-elimination surveillance across foci that have historically been affected will be crucial.

items.title: Simulating the risk of hPSC variants in scale-up versus scale-out culture.
items.abstract: Cancer-like genetic variants threaten bioreactor expansion of human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) for cell therapy manufacturing. Simulating scale-up versus scale-out, we find batch size, not master stock size, governs variant risk. Scale-out compartmentalizes risk and detects contamination sooner but amplifies rare variants. With risk factored, scale-out lowers hPSC manufacturing cost. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

items.title: Rescue of glutaric aciduria type I by GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase.
items.abstract: Glutaric aciduria type I (GA-1) is a severe metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency of glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GCDH), leading to accumulation of organic acids in the brain and resulting in striatal injury and progressive movement disorders. Although early diagnosis and dietary management reduce risk, one-third of patients still develop debilitating neurological complications. We previously demonstrated that liver-specific deletion of aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase (AASS), an upstream enzyme in lysine degradation, is a promising therapeutic strategy. Here, we tested an N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated siRNA against Aass. Treatment of neonatal Gcdh-/- mice rescued lethality and improved the brain pathology while reducing toxic metabolites in the brain and other organs. Serum biomarkers, including glutaric acid, 3-hydroxyglutaric acid, and glutarylcarnitine, predicted neurological outcomes, supporting their use for therapeutic monitoring. Although systemic metabolite concentrations declined, their urinary excretion remained elevated, consistent with a renal washout phenomenon and preserved excretory capacity. These findings demonstrate the potential of liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapy as a treatment for GA-1.

items.title: Thelazia callipaeda: an emerging zoonotic eyeworm from Asia to Europe and North America.
items.abstract: Thelazia callipaeda is an emerging zoonotic nematode transmitted by lachryphagous fruit flies to mammalian hosts, including dogs, cats, wild carnivores, and humans, with wildlife reservoirs having a major role in transmission. Once restricted to Asia, the parasite has expanded across many animal species in Europe and, in the past 10 years, in some locations in North America, raising veterinary and public health concerns. Ecological modelling, molecular epidemiology, and entomological findings support ongoing geographical expansion, driven primarily by animal movement and the presence of competent hosts and vectors across regions. Human infections (ie, thelaziasis) primarily present with unilateral conjunctivitis and ocular irritation but can progress to severe ocular disease if left untreated. Increasing reports in domestic and wild animals from newly affected regions, such as the eastern coast of the USA and the Baltic region, highlight the need for integrated surveillance, clinical awareness, molecular monitoring, and coordinated control strategies to mitigate further spread and zoonotic risk. This Review summarises knowledge of the biology, vector ecology, epidemiology, genetic diversity, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of thelaziasis.

items.title: Improving the treatment of invasive fungal infections: novel antifungal and host-directed therapies.
items.abstract: Invasive fungal infections continue to cause substantial morbidity and mortality despite antifungal therapy, and available antifungal drugs have pharmacological limitations, growing resistance, and socioeconomic issues. However, treatment of invasive fungal infections is at a turning point, with several drugs that have advanced substantially through the antifungal pipeline, including agents that are first-in-class antifungals. Clinical research is ongoing to expand antifungal treatment strategies, including combining systemic antifungal drug classes or adjunctive local antifungal drug administration. In addition, host-directed therapies that harness the immune system to target invasive fungal diseases are increasingly studied. In this Review, we provide an overview of novel antifungals and other new treatment approaches for invasive fungal infections.

items.title: Assessment of Ebola virus persistence in vitreous fluid of Ebola virus disease survivors with vitreoretinal disease in Sierra Leone: a cross-sectional study.

sections.objective: Uveitis is a known ocular manifestation in individuals who have survived Ebola virus disease (EVD). However, whether Ebola virus (EBOV; Orthoebolavirus zairense) persistence in vitreous fluid contributes to long-term sequelae of uveitis in EVD survivors remains unclear. We aimed to characterise the clinical findings and molecular and immunological findings in vitreous fluid from EVD survivors undergoing vitreoretinal surgery.
sections.methods: This cross-sectional study recruited EVD survivors (cohort 1), household close contacts of EVD survivors (cohort 2), and non-EVD patients with uveitis (cohort 3) from the Sierra Leone Ministry of Health's Department of Ophthalmology or from the ongoing Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and the Lowell and Ruth Gess Eye Hospital Ebola Survivor Study (SMILE Study). EVD survivor status was based on an Ebola treatment unit certificate and confirmation in the Sierra Leone Association of Ebola Survivors registry, as well as an anti-EBOV assay. Close contacts of EVD survivors were individuals who lived in the same household as patients with EVD during the acute stage of the disease. Non-EVD patients with uveitis were individuals with vitreoretinal disease indications who were anticipated to benefit from surgical intervention. All patients had a comprehensive ophthalmic examination and pars plana vitrectomy with collection of vitreous fluid. These samples were investigated for molecular detection of EBOV RNA via quantitative RT-PCR (qRT-PCR) and evaluation of Goldmann-Witmer coefficients (GWCs) to identify intraocular production of EBOV-binding antibodies. Statistical analyses were performed to compare basic ophthalmic variables, demographic data, and GWC between the three groups.
sections.results: From Jan 1, 2023, to Jan 1, 2024, a total of 25 patients (cohort 1 n=10, cohort 2 n=5, cohort 3 n=10) were enrolled. 13 (52%) patients were female, and median age was 39 years (IQR 34·0-53·5). The median time from EVD symptom onset to surgery was 108·5 months (IQR 103·8-110·8) in cohort 1, and the median time from close contact with a patient with EVD to surgery was 106·0 months (IQR 103·0-106·0) in cohort 2. EBOV RNA was detected by qRT-PCR in the vitreous fluid of two (20%) of ten EVD survivors. GWCs for EBOV glycoprotein IgG were significantly elevated (median 3·59, IQR 0·93-12·53, p<0·005 for between-group comparisons) in EVD survivors compared with those in close contacts (median 0, IQR 0-2·2) and patients with uveitis (median 0, IQR 0-0·62).
sections.conclusion: The detection of virus-specific immune responses and viral RNA at a median of 9 years after EVD diagnosis suggests long-term EBOV RNA persistence in the vitreous fluid of EVD survivors with vitreoretinal disease.

items.title: Bias and equity in large language model-based applications for health care: a scoping review.
items.abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into health care presents both opportunities for innovation and risks of perpetuating existing biases and health disparities. Although these concerns are widely discussed, a systematic understanding of the research landscape regarding bias and equity in LLM-based applications for health care remains limited, and few discussions have translated into actionable mitigation strategies. We conducted a Scoping Review to systematically map this landscape and identify key trends and gaps. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus for English-language articles published from Jan 1, 2018, to March 10, 2026. Our analysis of the 201 included studies revealed a strong focus on specific medical contexts and demographic factors and a predominant reliance on proprietary models that constrain transparency in bias evaluation. A disconnect exists between bias detection and mitigation, and the potential of LLMs to promote health equity remains underexplored. To realise a more coherent integration of bias mitigation and health equity objectives in health-care LLM development, the field needs large-scale, endpoint-driven studies grounded in real-world clinical workflows. Furthermore, we advocate for standardised multidimensional bias evaluation frameworks developed with support from professional societies and lifecycle bias governance across both proprietary and open-weight models to guide the safe and equitable integration of LLMs into health care globally.

items.title: Health-care professionals' experiences of caring for older adults across Europe and beyond: a multinational, multilingual qualitative analysis of a cross-sectional survey.

sections.objective: Population ageing is increasing the demand for care of older people; however, the workforce involved in geriatric care remains under-resourced. Evidence on professional attitudes of people caring for older adults relies largely on structured questionnaires, single-profession samples, and high-income settings and rarely captures how professionals themselves describe this work. We aimed to describe how health-care professionals across Europe and beyond experience caring for older adults and identify patterns to inform education and workforce policies.
sections.methods: This was a cross-sectional qualitative analysis of free-text responses to an optional open-ended item ("Please describe your thoughts and feelings on caring for older people") within a multinational, multilingual online survey fielded by the Cooperation in Science and Technology (COST) Action 21122 PROmoting GeRiAtric Medicine in countries where it is still eMergING (PROGRAMMING) network. The survey was developed in English, translated into 24 languages, and disseminated online between Oct 9, 2023, and June 5, 2024. The survey was open to anyone whose work involved the care of older people. Participation was voluntary and anonymous. Gender was self-reported as man, woman, or prefer not to say; race and ethnicity data were not collected. Responses with fewer than three words were considered non-interpretable and excluded. Native speaker members of the author team coded responses in their original languages using inductive reflexive thematic content analysis, followed by integrative cross-thematic synthesis in English. Reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines.
sections.results: 2196 (40·1%) of 5474 professionals from 60 countries or territories provided analysable responses in 25 languages for the free-text item. Most (1733 [78·9%] of 2196) respondents were from Europe. 436 (19·8%) respondents were from western Asia-predominantly Türkiye (378 [17·2%] of 2196)-and 27 (1·2%) of 2196 were from elsewhere. By qualitatively analysing these responses, we identified seven broad themes that reflected the shared patterns and tensions of the professionals involved in geriatric care. One theme was identified as the overarching pattern within which the remaining six themes were positioned. Three of the remaining themes (themes 2, 4, and 7) described the individual experiences of the work, whereas themes 3, 5, and 6 described the systemic context of the work. Professionals described intrinsic reward and personal growth through relational care, alongside moral distress from systemic neglect, resource scarcity, educational gaps, and low professional standing. Emotional labour was foundational yet largely invisible. Respect, empathy, patience, and compassion were the most frequently cited values, recognised as core competencies rather than as personal traits.
sections.conclusion: Professionals reported the care systems themselves to be the main obstacle to good care for older people; this pattern recurred across professions, countries, and economies. Policies should move beyond increasing headcount to recognising the emotional labour and resilience of the workforce and restructuring health systems to advance age-friendly care.

items.title: Natural ligand-based CAR T-cell therapy targeting BCMA and TACI for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (TriPRIL): a non-randomised, phase 1, first-in-human trial.

sections.objective: Functional loss of B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a recognised mechanism of relapse after BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Targeting multiple tumour antigens simultaneously with a single CAR has the potential to mitigate antigen escape and prolong disease responses. Transmembrane activator and CAML interactor (TACI) and BCMA are both highly expressed on most myeloma cells and bind to the same natural ligand-a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL). We designed TriPRIL, a CAR that uses an engineered trimeric form of APRIL, to target both BCMA and TACI. We aimed to establish the safety, tolerability, preliminary efficacy, and recommended phase 2 dose of autologous TriPRIL CAR T cells.
sections.methods: In this first-in-human, open-label, dose-escalation and dose-expansion, phase 1 study, we evaluated TriPRIL in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at Massachusetts General Hospital (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients had received at least three previous lines of therapy or had triple-class refractory disease. Previous CAR T-cell therapy and bispecific antibody therapy exposure were permitted. Patients received 3 days of lymphodepletion with intravenous cyclophosphamide (300 mg/m2) and intravenous fludarabine (30 mg/m2) daily on days -5, -4, and -3 before intravenous TriPRIL infusion on day 0. In the dose escalation phase, patients received 1·0 × 108 or 3·0 × 108 TriPRIL CAR T cells to establish the recommended phase 2 dose, which was further evaluated in the dose expansion phase. The primary endpoint was the incidence of study-related adverse events (graded according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5) and dose-limiting toxicities in all patients who received an infusion of TriPRIL CAR T cells, until study completion at 24 months or progressive disease. The data cutoff date was March 24, 2026, when all infused patients had completed at least one assessment of disease response. This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05020444), has fully accrued, and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Sept 17, 2021, and Jan 27, 2026, 16 patients were enrolled and underwent leukapheresis, with 15 patients subsequently receiving a TriPRIL cell infusion. Ten (67%) of 15 infused patients were female, five (33%)were male, and the median age was 69 years (IQR 65-75). Nine (60%) of 15 infused patients had previously received BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy, and four (27%) had previously received a BCMA-directed or GPRC5D-directed bispecific T-cell engager. Six patients were treated with 1·0 × 108 CAR T cells, and nine were treated with 3·0 × 108 CAR T cells; there were no dose-limiting toxicities at either dose. The most common adverse events were neutropenia (14 [93%] of 15 patients), nausea (12 [80%]), hypogammaglobulinaemia (eight [53%]), fatigue (seven [47%]), and fever (seven [47%]). Non-haematological adverse events grade 3 or worse occurred in five (33%) patients and all resolved. Cytokine release syndrome (grade 1 or 2 only) occurred in 13 (87%, 95% CI 60-98) infused patients. One (7%, 0-32) patient had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, and one (7%, 0-32) had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like syndrome; both of these patients had received 3·0 × 108 CAR T cells, and both conditions resolved with corticosteroids. Infections occurred in six (40%, 16-68) infused patients, with a grade 3 infection in one patient (7%, 0-32). There were no treatment-related deaths. The recommended phase 2 dose of CAR T cells was set as 3·0 × 108 cells.
sections.conclusion: TriPRIL showed a favourable safety profile and warrants further investigation in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, including those previously treated with BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy. The study findings support further development of this dual-targeted, natural ligand-based CAR T-cell approach.

items.title: Paleogenomics illuminates mobility and changing lifeways in Chalcolithic Anatolia.
items.abstract: Once labeled the "Dark Ages" of Anatolian prehistory, the Chalcolithic period (c. 6000-3000 BCE) was characterized by drastically reduced settlement densities compared with the preceding Neolithic and the succeeding Bronze Ages, a change interpreted as population decline. Using 44 new genomes combined with published data, we find no evidence for a population reduction. The genetic evidence instead suggests that populations in Chalcolithic Anatolia were increasingly mobile and/or growing in size while receiving gene flow from eastern regions (e.g., East Anatolia and the South Caucasus) through a 3,000-year-long admixture process. We propose that genetic and archaeological evidence may be reconciled by hypothesizing the presence of communities with dispersed and mobile lifeways that are mostly invisible to archaeology. These communities also practiced consanguinity at frequencies unobserved in previous periods. Finally, we identify a mid-5th-millennium BCE individual in Central Anatolia carrying ∼10%-30% Pontic-Caspian Steppe-related ancestry, shedding light on mobility between the Eurasian Steppe and Anatolia.

items.title: Evolutionary repurposing of a pore-forming toxin drives epithelial remodeling during terrestrial adaptation.
items.abstract: The ability of vertebrates to conquer land is attributed to innovations in respiration and locomotion. However, land adaptation profoundly reshaped mucosal surfaces such as the skin, the main interface between hosts and the environment. To adapt to land, African lungfish annually remodel their skin, forming a cocoon. Here, we report the discovery of a small pore-forming toxin in African lungfish, Protop-CrTX-A, with no other vertebrate counterpart that is sufficient to drive epithelial morphogenesis transcriptional programs. In free-swimming lungfish, goblet cells secrete Protop-CrTX-A into the mucus. During estivation, this niche is replaced by a mucin-low/basal epithelial niche, adjacent to a granulocyte immune niche that becomes the predominant source of Protop-CrTX-A in the estivated skin. Protop-CrTX-A acts as a reversible switch for skin remodeling, sufficient to convert African lungfish skin between aquatic and terrestrial states. We propose that innate immunity, through its capacity to remodel tissues, was a key driver of vertebrate water-land transitions.

items.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Super-High-Pressure Noncompliant Balloons for Treatment of Calcified Coronary Lesions: The VICTORY Trial.

sections.objective: Although calcified coronary lesions are associated with poor outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI), randomized data guiding lesion preparation are limited. Small studies suggest potential benefits of super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons (SH-NCB); however, they have not been directly compared with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). The goal of this study was to conduct a randomized comparison of SH-NCBs vs IVL in calcified lesions.
sections.methods: In this open-label, randomized controlled, noninferiority trial with blinded outcomes assessment (ie, the PROBE design), patients aged ≥18 years with calcified coronary lesions were randomly assigned (1:1) to undergo lesion preparation with SH-NCBs or IVL before PCI with drug-eluting stents. All patients were required to undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary endpoint was final stent expansion (%) according to OCT. Secondary endpoints included procedural success, strategy success, target vessel failure, stent expansion <80%, and safety outcomes (eg, coronary perforation).
sections.results: Between December 21, 2022, and August 11, 2025, a total of 278 patients underwent the randomly assigned study procedure using plaque modification with SH-NCBs or IVL before stent implantation. The majority of patients (68%) had severe calcium based on an OCT Fujino score ≥4. Study procedures involving IVL tended to be longer and require more auxiliary devices compared with SH-NCBs. The median pressure applied with SH-NCBs compared with IVL was 40 atmospheres vs 6 atmospheres. Regarding the primary endpoint of stent expansion, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL (85% vs 84%; Pnoninferiority < 0.0001). The results were consistent across all subgroups, including calcium severity. Use of SH-NCBs, compared with IVL, resulted in similar rates of procedural and strategy success. Safety outcomes, specifically coronary perforations, did not differ between the 2 groups. At 30 days' follow-up, target vessel failure events (including cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, or myocardial infarction) occurred in 4 (2.8%) patients in the SH-NCB group and in 8 (5.7%) patients in the IVL group (HR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15 to 1.66; P = 0.26).
sections.conclusion: In calcified coronary lesions, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL for stent expansion and exhibited a comparable safety profile in experienced operators using intravascular imaging. (Value of IVL Compared To OPN Non-Compliant Balloons for Treatment of Refractory Coronary Lesions [VICTORY]; NCT05346068).

items.title: OCTA-Derived predictors of reactivation in quiescent type 1 macular neovascularisation: A longitudinal real-world cohort study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the activation rate of quiescent type 1 macular neovascularisation (MNV) and to identify optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-derived predictors of conversion to exudative disease.
sections.methods: A retrospective longitudinal cohort study was conducted in eyes with treatment-naïve quiescent MNV associated with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) or polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV). The study duration was from Jan 2012 to December 2025. Structural OCT and OCTA parameters were analysed at baseline and during follow-up. Activation was defined as the development of intraretinal or subretinal fluid or haemorrhage requiring anti-VEGF therapy. Statistical analyses included Fisher's exact test, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.
sections.results: Among 50 eyes with quiescent MNV, 17 (34%) progressed to exudative disease over a mean follow-up of 35.9 months. Significant predictors of activation included neovascular area enlargement (OR 23.83, 95% CI 3.35-169.39, p = 0.001), hypointense halo formation on OCTA (OR 20.00, 95% CI 2.04-196.37, p = 0.004), increased branching complexity (OR 16.25, 95% CI 2.46-107.24, p = 0.003), and increasing pigment epithelial detachment (PED) dimensions (OR 12.50, 95% CI 2.11-74.20, p = 0.004). The mean duration of quiescence prior to activation was 48.6 months.
sections.conclusion: OCTA-derived vascular remodelling features are strong predictors of activation in quiescent type 1 MNV. Incorporating these biomarkers into clinical surveillance protocols may improve risk stratification and enable earlier detection of conversion.

items.title: Epidemiology and Modifiable Risk Factors for Benign Prostatic Enlargement and Related Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.

sections.conclusion: BPE and related LUTS represent highly prevalent health issues with global incidence and prevalence rates projected to increase in the next decade. Positive associations between high adiposity indices and prevalent BPE have been observed in both Asian and non-Asian males. Modifiable risk factors associated with moderate-to-severe LUTS include: abnormal adiposity indices, levels of physical activity, smoking status, alcohol intake, metabolic syndrome (all in both ethnicities), and sleep/dietary patterns (in Asian males). However, definitive clinical recommendations could not be provided.
sections.other: Benign prostatic enlargement (BPE) and related lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS/BPE) represent highly prevalent health issues globally, and related modifiable risk factors are recognized as a sensitive topic for prevention strategies. We summarized evidence on associations between the epidemiology of these conditions and modifiable risk factors. We performed a systematic review with meta-analysis of studies in MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols. Twenty-four studies (four cohort and 20 cross-sectional) were included. Pooled synthesis showed positive associations between waist circumference (WC) >90 cm (two studies) and body mass index >24 kg/m2 (three studies) and prevalent BPE in Asian males. WC >90 cm was positively associated with prevalent moderate-to-severe LUTS in the same ethnicity (two studies). Narrative synthesis showed associations between abnormal adiposity and prevalent BPE/moderate-to-severe LUTS also in non-Asian males as well as associations between the epidemiology of LUTS and physical activity, alcohol intake, metabolic syndrome, and smoking status in both ethnicities. Associations between dietary/sleep patterns and LUTS epidemiology were evident in Asian males. The certainty of evidence was very low.

items.title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.

sections.objective: To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.
sections.methods: This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.
sections.results: In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).
sections.conclusion: Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

items.title: Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair as a Salvage Strategy after Failed Chimney Endovascular Aortic Repair: An International Multicentre Cohort.

sections.objective: Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.
sections.methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 29 consecutive patients (median age 81.0 years, interquartile range [IQR] 66.0, 83.0) treated across 13 European centres (2013 - 2025) for failed chEVAR using branched endografts. The primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day clinical success, and procedure related complications. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, freedom from re-intervention, and target visceral vessel (TVV) patency.
sections.results: The median interval from index chEVAR to BEVAR re-intervention was 48.5 months (IQR 30.0, 80.8). Acute urgent or emergent procedures accounted for 17% of cases (n = 5), while 31% (n = 9) underwent expedited repair for large aneurysms. Off the shelf devices were utilised in 41% of cases. A total of 106 TVVs were incorporated through branches, with a mean of 3.7 vessels per patient. Technical success was achieved in 97% (28 of 29). There was no peri-operative mortality or open surgical conversion. Significant complications included two cases (7%) of severe spinal cord ischaemia. The thirty day clinical success rate was 90%. At a median follow up of 19 months (IQR 9, 40), the Kaplan-Meier estimate for overall survival was 92% at 1 year. TVV patency was 100%, with only one renal artery re-intervention for in stent re-stenosis. Freedom from branch related re-intervention was 96% at 1 year.
sections.conclusion: Salvage of failed chEVAR using branched endografts is technically demanding but yields excellent early results. In experienced centres, BEVAR appears feasible and offers one potential salvage option in selected patients with suitable anatomy, particularly when an off the shelf solution is required.

items.title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.

sections.objective: This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).
sections.methods: Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.
sections.results: Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.
sections.conclusion: A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

items.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Telemedicine Questionnaire Visits for Post-Operative Strabismus Patients.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness, patient satisfaction, and estimated travel burden reduction associated with telemedicine post-operative week one (POW1) follow-up after strabismus surgery.
sections.methods: Retrospective observational case series. Patients selected for telemedicine follow-up completed an electronic questionnaire assessing postoperative well-being, diplopia status, and medication adherence, and uploaded ocular photographs for subsequent clinician review. A subset of patients completed a telephone satisfaction survey assessing usability and overall experience.
sections.results: Of 201 patients, 183 completed telemedicine follow-up without an in-person POW1 visit. Overall, 98.4% reported feeling well postoperatively, 66.7% reported complete resolution of diplopia, and 90.7% reported adherence to prescribed medications. Common free-text response themes included reassurance with recovery, expected postoperative symptoms, visual concerns, and questions regarding postoperative care. Twenty-eight patients completed a satisfaction survey, demonstrating high ratings for ease of use, comfort with the platform, and willingness to use the process again. All respondents agreed that telemedicine follow-up saved time compared with a traditional in-person visit. Telemedicine follow-up was associated with an estimated potential travel reduction of 46,249 miles (mean, 252.7 miles per patient). No postoperative complications were identified among patients managed exclusively through telemedicine follow-up.
sections.conclusion: Telemedicine POW1 follow-up was feasible in selected strabismus patients, with high satisfaction among telephone survey respondents and substantial estimated potential travel avoidance. These findings support further evaluation of telemedicine follow-up as an alternative to routine in-person POW1 visits in appropriately selected patients.
sections.other: A total of 201 patients (age range, 2-83 years of age) who underwent strabismus surgery at a single tertiary academic center between March 2020 and February 2026 and completed an electronic POW1 questionnaire. Patient-reported postoperative well-being, diplopia status, medication adherence, post-operative complications, patient satisfaction, and estimated travel avoidance.

items.title: A cell-type-resolved proteomic atlas reveals intra- and intercellular signaling in Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) arises from pathological interactions among diverse brain cell types, but cell-type-specific proteomic changes remain underexplored. Here, we present deep proteomic profiling of sorted or proximity-labeled brain cells from AD mouse models (5xFAD and AppNL-G-F) at multiple ages, quantifying 13,411 proteins in microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocyte precursor cells, and neurons, with additional spatial information. We identified 3,028 differentially abundant proteins, most of which were absent in a bulk proteomic dataset, and constructed cell-type-specific networks to define functional modules and hub proteins. Comparison with transcriptomic data revealed that ∼30% of proteomic changes are RNA discordant. Further analyses uncovered cross-cell-type signaling proteins conserved in human AD brains, such as pleiotrophin (Ptn), which is transcriptionally enriched in astrocytes but accumulates in microglia. Importantly, recombinant PTN activates human induced microglia (iMG) cells. Thus, these findings provide a comprehensive cell-type-resolved proteomic atlas of AD models, highlighting novel intra- and intercellular signaling events.

items.title: Hedgehog Signaling-Dependent Heterochronic Control of Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Establishes Distinct Cardiac Progenitor Fields.

sections.objective: The mammalian heart is formed from distinct cardiac progenitor fields: the first heart field (FHF), second heart field (SHF), and juxta-cardiac field (JCF). How these fields are established remains one of the oldest questions in cardiac biology and is central to understanding congenital heart disease, which differentially affects derivatives of the individual fields. Previous work has demonstrated that the fields emerge and differentiate at distinct times; however, the mechanisms underlying their establishment have remained elusive. Here, we implicate Hedgehog signaling-dependent heterochronic control of cardiac differentiation in the emergence of different heart fields.
sections.methods: We assessed Hedgehog signaling activity by assembling a cardio-mesodermal single-cell atlas. We analyzed Hedgehog ligand gene expression by confocal imaging in gastrulating mouse embryos. We investigated the necessity of Hedgehog signaling using 2 distinct genetic Hedgehog loss-of-function mouse models, analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis.
sections.results: Our results show that Hedgehog signaling mediates field-specific heterochronic control of differentiation timing that orchestrates the establishment of the SHF and JCF as distinct from the FHF. We identify a common cardiac progenitor transcriptomic state from which all 3 fields emerge. We show that the SHF and JCF are established coincident with Hedgehog signaling reception, whereas the FHF evades Hedgehog pathway activity and rapidly differentiates. We find that Hedgehog ligand expression sandwiches the cardiac mesoderm emerging from the primitive streak, spatially coordinating SHF and JCF establishment. Partial depletion of Hedgehog signaling causes premature activation of the cardiac differentiation program in the SHF and JCF. Complete ablation of Hedgehog signaling results in failed SHF and JCF establishment.
sections.conclusion: Our findings reveal a Hedgehog signaling-dependent, non-cell-autonomous heterochronic mechanism required for SHF and JCF formation. This heterochronic mechanism provides a new paradigm for understanding the ordered temporal emergence of the cardiac progenitor fields that support the development of the 4-chambered heart, as well as a general model for the emergence of progenitor fields that drive organogenesis across the mammalian body plan.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

items.title: Intracoronary Imaging-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

sections.objective: Recent societal guidelines provide a Class I recommendation for intracoronary imaging (ICI)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for complex or left main coronary artery disease; however, recent trials have failed to show a benefit. The study aim was to re-evaluate the efficacy of ICI-guided PCI and to explore heterogeneity of results across trials.
sections.methods: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases were searched through June 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing outcomes with ICI-guided PCI vs angiography-guided PCI in the drug-eluting stent era. Direct comparison meta-analyses, mixed treatment comparison meta-analyses, trial sequential analyses, fragility analysis, and Bayesian meta-analyses were performed. Meta-regression analysis was performed to evaluate heterogeneity using the following variables: stent length (surrogate for lesion length), stent diameter, difference in postdilatation (percentage) between the groups, publication year, and geographic location.
sections.results: A total of 28 RCTs met the inclusion criteria, comprising 24,634 patients (mean age 64.8 years; 75.9% male) with a mean follow-up of 22 months. ICI-guided PCI reduced target lesion failure (relative risk [RR]: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.61-0.85; I2 = 61%), cardiac mortality (RR: 0.73; 0.58-0.91; I2 = 5%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86; 0.75-0.97; I2 = 0%), target vessel revascularization (RR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.57-0.83, I2 = 41%), stent thrombosis (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.40-0.76; I2 = 0%), and all-cause mortality (RR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.70-0.96; I2 = 0%) compared with angiography-guided PCI. Trial sequential analysis confirmed evidence for at least a 20% reduction in all outcomes with ICI-guided PCI. The fragility index was robust, ranging from 9 to 50. The posterior probability for benefit was >99% for all outcomes. Trial differences in geography and lesion characteristics explained most of the between-trial variance (residual tau = 0).
sections.conclusion: In this updated meta-analysis of RCTs, after accounting for modifier effects from recent studies, ICI-guided PCI was associated with significantly reduced cardiovascular events compared with angiography-guided PCI. Geographic heterogeneity across trials was present mainly for target vessel revascularization, explained in large part by differences in lesion characteristics and procedural technique.

items.title: Stent Retriever Thrombectomy in Patients With Myocardial Infarction: The Open-Label, Multicenter NATURE Superiority Trial.

sections.objective: Patients with myocardial infarction and large thrombus burden face greater infarct size and higher mortality; yet, no effective therapy exists for this high-risk subgroup. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of stent-retriever thrombectomy in addition to conventional percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) vs conventional PCI alone on infarct size.
sections.methods: In this open-label, multicenter, superiority trial, 160 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and large thrombus burden at angiography (TIMI [Thrombolysis In Myocardial Infarction] thrombus flow grade ≥3 in infarct-related artery) were consented, and 156 were randomly assigned to undergo stent-retriever thrombectomy followed by conventional PCI or conventional PCI alone. Primary outcome was infarct size extension assessed by area under the curve for creatine kinase-MB. Safety outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (comprising cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke) at 3 and 30 days.
sections.results: Infarct size (creatine kinase-MB area under the curve) was lower in the stent-retriever group (n = 78) vs the conventional group (n = 76) (3,965 IU/L·h; Q1-Q3: 2,480-5,092 IU/L·h vs 5,250 IU/L·h; Q1-Q3: 3,506-7,449 IU/L·h; difference -1,359; 95% CI: -2,231 to -522; P = 0.001). At exploratory cardiac magnetic resonance findings, infarct size was lower in the stent-retriever group (n = 64; left ventricle, 17%; Q1-Q3: 11%-28%) vs the conventional PCI group (n = 59; 28.0%; Q1-Q3: 18%-33%; difference -7.0; 95% CI: -12 to -2.0), whereas left ventricular volumes and ejection fraction did not differ. There were no major adverse cardiovascular events at 3 days and 1 at 30 days in the stent-retriever group vs 2 and 3 major adverse cardiovascular events, respectively, in the conventional PCI group.
sections.conclusion: Stent-retriever thrombectomy followed by conventional PCI in patients with large thrombus burden undergoing primary PCI ≤8 hours of symptom onset was associated with reduced infarct size vs conventional PCI alone. (NATURE [EnVast as an Adjunct PPCI in Subjects Presenting With STEMI]; NCT04969471).

items.title: Addition of Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve in the Diagnostic Pathway of Patients With Stable Coronary Artery Disease: The FUSION Randomized Controlled Trial.

sections.objective: Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFRct) integrates anatomical and functional information, which is particularly useful for stable coronary artery disease (CAD) patients with at least intermediate stenosis. We investigated the impact of adding FFRct to the diagnostic pathway of CAD patients with a 50% to 90% stenosis on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA).
sections.methods: FUSION is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized controlled trial involving patients with 50% to 90% stenosis in ≥1 coronary artery on CCTA. Patients were randomized to FFRct-guided or usual care. The primary endpoint was invasive coronary angiography (ICA) without obstructive CAD at 90 days. Secondary endpoints included ICA without obstructive CAD, major adverse cardiac events, and costs at 1 year, as well as revascularizations, and quality of life at 90 days and 1 year. ICA use was assessed as a post hoc exploratory endpoint.
sections.results: Overall, 528 patients (median age: 63 years [25th-75th: 57-69 years]; 59% male) were randomized to FFRct-guided (n = 263) or usual care (n = 265). At 90 days, the rate of ICA without obstructive CAD was significantly lower in the FFRct group than in the usual care group (18% [48 of 263] vs 33% [87 of 265]; OR: 0.46; 95% CI: 0.31-0.69; P < 0.001). ICA rate was 39% (102 of 263) vs 51% (136 of 265), respectively (P = 0.004). Both differences persisted at 1 year. Revascularization rates were similar: 20% (52 of 263) vs 20% (53 of 265) at 1 year, respectively (P = 0.948). Quality of life, costs, and major adverse cardiac events did not differ between groups, although the clinical event rates were low.
sections.conclusion: Adding FFRct to the diagnostic pathway of patients with a 50% to 90% stenosis on CCTA reduced the rate of ICA without obstructive CAD at 90 days and 1 year, without differences in revascularizations, quality of life, and costs compared with usual care. Clinical event rates were similar, although low. The rate of overall ICA use, a post hoc exploratory outcome, was also reduced at 90 days and 1 year.

items.title: Pulmonary Artery Pressures Predict Heart Failure Events Following Heart Failure and Non-Heart Failure Events.

sections.objective: It is uncertain whether pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) within the first week after either hospitalization for a non-heart failure event (HFE) or hospitalization or urgent visit for a HFE predicts the risk of recurring events. This study aims to determine if PAP following a non-HFE or HFE predicts subsequent events within 90 days.
sections.methods: The authors examined non-HFE and HFE in patients with heart failure (HF) treated with remote hemodynamic-guided management using a wireless PAP sensor in the GUIDE-HF study. They compared PAP trends before and after a non-HFE or HFE and stratified the admitting and discharge PAP during the index event into groups with a subsequent HFE, non-HFE, or no further events within 90 days.
sections.results: Following index non-HFE (615 events, n = 425), post-discharge diastolic PAP was significantly higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.3 ± 7.9 mm Hg) (n = 97) vs patients with a subsequent non-HFE (20.4 ± 7.3 mm Hg; P = 0.0046) (n = 189) or no further events (20.9 ± 7.4 mm Hg; P = 0.015) (n = 329). Following index HFE (539 events, n = 358), post-discharge diastolic PAP was numerically higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.9 ± 6.9 mm Hg) (n = 199) than in patients with a subsequent non-HFE (22.0 ± 7.1 mm Hg; P = 0.078 (n = 102) and in those with no further events (22.0 ± 7.6 mm Hg; P = 0.021) (n = 238). Similar trends were observed for HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction subgroups and with systolic and mean PAP.
sections.conclusion: Persistently elevated PAP early after discharge following either an index non-HFE or an HFE is associated with the risk of a subsequent HFE. (Hemodynamic-GUIDEd Management of Heart Failure [GUIDE-HF]; NCT03387813).

items.title: Efficacy and safety of upadacitinib in Takayasu arteritis (SELECT-TAK): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: For patients with Takayasu arteritis, a rare large-vessel vasculitis, there remains an unmet need for immunosuppressive treatments that reduce reliance on long-term glucocorticoids and maintain remission. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of upadacitinib, an oral JAK inhibitor, for the treatment of Takayasu arteritis.
sections.methods: SELECT-TAK is a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 31 tertiary referral centres and university hospitals in six countries (Japan, China, South Korea, Argentina, Brazil, and Türkiye). Eligibility criteria included patients aged 18 years or older (aged ≥15 years in Japan) with Takayasu arteritis who had at least one unsuccessful attempt at glucocorticoid tapering, relapsed within 12 weeks of baseline, and were in remission with a stable glucocorticoid dose less than or equal to 1 mg/kg per day for at least 1 week before baseline. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral upadacitinib 15 mg or placebo once daily, with all patients following a glucocorticoid taper starting at week 4 (10% per week to at least 0·1 mg/kg per day). Treatment assignment was masked from investigators, patients, study site personnel, and study sponsor. The primary endpoint was the time to first relapse during the double-blind period, as defined by fulfilling the criteria of signs and symptoms in two of five categories (ie, objective systemic symptoms, subjective systemic symptoms, elevated inflammation markers, vascular signs and symptoms, or ischaemic symptoms) at two consecutive assessments or at one assessment when urgent treatment escalation was required. Efficacy and safety analyses included all patients who received at least one dose of the study drug. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04161898) and is active but not recruiting. Individuals with lived experience were not involved in the study design or implementation.
sections.results: Between March 3, 2020, and Dec 5, 2023, 59 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to receive upadacitinib (n=30) or placebo (n=29). The mean age was 38·2 years (SD 16·1), with most patients (35 [59%]) younger than 40 years. 53 (90%) patients were female and six (10%) were male. The majority of patients were Asian (44 [75%]), with the largest proportion being Japanese (36 [61%]). The primary endpoint was not met with upadacitinib (hazard ratio 0·52, 95% CI 0·24-1·12; log-rank test p=0·045). Median time to relapse was 107·9 weeks (95% CI 20·1-not estimable) with upadacitinib versus 20·1 weeks (12·0-127·1) with placebo. 11 (37%) relapse events occurred in 30 patients in the upadacitinib group and 18 (62%) occurred in 29 patients in the placebo group. Nine serious adverse events were reported with upadacitinib and four with placebo; no deaths were reported in either group.
sections.conclusion: The primary endpoint was not met; the time to first relapse analysis numerically favoured upadacitinib over placebo, but did not meet the prespecified statistical significance threshold. No new clinically meaningful safety events were identified. Further exploration of upadacitinib in refractory Takayasu arteritis is warranted.

items.title: Robotic versus open pancreatoduodenectomy: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Robotic pancreatoduodenectomy aims to enhance patient recovery compared with open pancreatoduodenectomy. Although randomised controlled trials report similar major morbidity between approaches, these studies are underpowered to detect low-frequency outcomes and treatment effect in patient subgroups. Therefore, this study aimed to compare patient outcomes following robotic pancreatoduodenectomy versus open pancreatoduodenectomy across subgroups.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis, we searched Ovid Medline, Embase, Web of Science (Core Collection), and the Cochrane Library from database inception to July 3, 2026, for randomised controlled trials comparing robotic versus open pancreatoduodenectomy. Non-randomised studies, studies comparing only laparoscopic to open pancreatoduodenectomy, and trials which did not report on the outcomes of interest were excluded. The principal investigators of all trials agreed to collaborate and share individual patient data. Primary outcomes were major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥3) and modified time to functional recovery (mTTFR). This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251034123).
sections.results: The search identified 3415 studies. 1687 remained after removal of duplication. After screening, four trials involving 25 experienced, high-volume centres across seven countries were eligible for inclusion. Three trials showed some concerns of bias, while one trial was of low risk. These trials included 745 patients who had undergone pancreatoduodenectomy for all indications (412 [55%] who had robotic pancreatoduodenectomy and 333 [45%] who had open pancreatoduodenectomy). Of the 744 patients with available baseline characteristic data, 298 (40%) were female, (60%) were male, and the median age was 65 years (IQR 57-72). Major complications occurred in 140 (34%) of 407 patients after robotic pancreatoduodenectomy and 106 (32%) of 329 patients after open pancreatoduodenectomy (adjusted risk difference -2% [95% CI -7 to 3], padjusted=0·37; tau2<0·0001). Median mTTFR was 9 days (IQR 6-14) after robotic pancreatoduodenectomy and 12 days (7-15) after open pancreatoduodenectomy (adjusted median difference -2 [95% CI -3 to -1]; padjusted<0·0001; tau2=0·16). In exploratory subgroup analyses, there was no evidence for treatment effect heterogeneity in terms of major complications and mTTFR based on age, obesity, and fistula risk, or by the presence of fistula.
sections.conclusion: This individual patient data meta-analysis of four randomised controlled trials provides the highest level evidence to date on robotic pancreatoduodenectomy and confirms that the robotic approach is a safe alternative to open pancreatoduodenectomy in terms of major morbidity and mortality, with a 2-day faster recovery in experienced, high-volume centres.

items.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in surgically resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (PRIME-HCC): a prospective, phase 1b, single-arm trial and translational analyses.

sections.objective: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment.
sections.methods: PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population.
