Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing.
sections.results: Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells.
sections.conclusion: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation.

items.title: Wear time matters: optimising wearables for clinically aligned and personalised health monitoring.
items.abstract: Wearable devices hold transformative potential for healthcare, yet their clinical impact is undermined by suboptimal long-term adherence. Although 24/7 always-on monitoring remains the default for maximising data completeness, achieving sustained wear could be limited by discomfort, inconvenience, or perceived lack of relevance, particularly during longitudinal monitoring. The clinical utility of wearables also depends on intelligent systems that filter, contextualise, and prioritise the resulting data into timely and actionable insights for individuals and clinicians. In this Viewpoint, we reframe wear time as a strategic design opportunity rather than a technical requirement. We provide illustrative examples of varying wear time requirements across clinical contexts: for instance, continuous monitoring is valuable for detecting intermittent episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, whereas periodic blood pressure monitoring may be appropriate for managing stable hypertension. Our systemic analysis identified nine interconnected dimensions influencing wear time adherence, spanning clinical contexts, human factors, and technological reliability. Building on these insights, we propose a strategic implementation framework grounded in human-centred design, adaptive precision, and intelligent engagement. By aligning wear time strategies with specific clinical contexts and individual characteristics, wearables can evolve from passive data collectors into personalised health companions that balance clinical precision with real-world usability, fostering sustainable adherence and clinically meaningful insights.

items.title: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core.
items.abstract: Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

items.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age.

sections.objective: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking.
sections.methods: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68.
sections.results: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group.
sections.conclusion: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).

items.title: Immersive Reality in Cardiothoracic Surgical Education.
items.abstract: Immersive reality technologies, including virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality, and related extended reality platforms, are reforming how surgeons learn complex anatomy, rehearse procedures, develop technical skills, and manage unexpected or rare intraoperative crises. Cardiothoracic surgery is particularly well suited to these tools because postgraduate training occurs in a high-stakes environment characterized by complex 3-dimensional anatomy, limited operative exposure, minimally invasive/robotic approaches, open communication, and the need for synchronized team performance. Immersive platforms facilitate anatomy education and procedural planning and enable deliberate practice and nontechnical skills training. Although most studies remain small, heterogeneous, and focused on surrogate outcomes rather than patient outcomes, evidence from surgical education and cardiothoracic surgery literature demonstrates that these tools impart improvement in knowledge, confidence, procedural accuracy, and simulator performance. This article defines immersive reality technologies, reviews their educational rationale and emerging applications in cardiothoracic surgery, proposes an implementation framework for training programs, and highlights limitations related to haptics, validation, privacy, equity, and regulatory oversight. The next phase should focus on validation of outcome-linked curricula that integrate immersive simulation into competency-based surgical education.

items.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.

sections.objective: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.
sections.methods: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.
sections.results: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death.
sections.conclusion: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies.

items.title: Biatrial Versus Left Atrial Maze Ablation During Cardiac Valve Surgery for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The ABLATION Trial.

sections.objective: Guidelines recommend concomitant surgical ablation during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the optimal lesion set remains uncertain, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits and risks of biatrial versus left atrial (LA) maze ablation.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, randomized, single-blind trial, patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic mitral valve surgery, with or without concomitant cardiac surgical procedures, were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo biatrial or LA maze ablation. The biatrial group underwent a complete Cox-Maze IV procedure; the LA group received a left-sided maze lesion set. To ensure standardization and consistency of the ablation procedures, surgeons underwent pretrial training and certification, and all procedures were videorecorded and centrally reviewed. The primary outcome was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias lasting >30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs within 12 months. The key secondary end point was freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation.
sections.results: All 323 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 56.5 years; 72.1% women; mean LA diameter, 51.9 mm). At 12 months, 78.7% of patients (129 of 164) in the biatrial group and 68.6% (109 of 159) in the LA group were free from atrial tachyarrhythmias (adjusted difference, 10.7% [1-sided lower 95% CI, 3%]; P=0.01). Freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation was noted in 97.0% (159 of 164) of the biatrial group and 98.1% (156 of 159) of the LA group, meeting the predefined noninferiority criterion with a margin of -5% (adjusted difference, -1.1% [1-sided lower 95% CI, -3.9%]; Pnoninferiority=0.01).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic cardiac valve surgery, biatrial maze ablation was superior to LA maze ablation in reducing recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmias, while maintaining noninferiority with respect to permanent pacemaker implantation. These findings provide direct evidence to inform lesion-set selection for surgical ablation during cardiac surgery.

items.title: Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: From Prolapse to Precision Therapy.
items.abstract: Degenerative mitral valve regurgitation due to mitral valve prolapse affects ≈15 million people globally and is the commonest indication for mitral intervention in high-income countries, but its biology, natural history, and lifetime management are ill defined. This review summarizes current knowledge of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and lifetime management of degenerative mitral regurgitation, with a focus on areas of uncertainty, recent advances, and emerging research directions. These include translational research focused on determining genetic and cellular drivers of disease progression and mechanistic studies geared to improve detection and prevention of downstream myocardial dysfunction, particularly in high-risk phenotypes, including arrhythmic mitral prolapse. The current landscape of randomized trials and large registries comparing contemporary surgical and transcatheter treatment and strategies to improve patient access to care and outcomes across all patient risk profiles and populations are also discussed.

items.title: Spectral envelopes of facial movements predict intention, cortical representations, and neural prosthetic control.
items.abstract: Animals use coordinated facial movements to sample the environment, ingest nutrients, and communicate. Rodents produce rhythmic facial movements during spontaneous behavior and cognitive tasks. Measuring these movements precisely and linking them to neural activity remains challenging. We introduce face-rhythm, an unsupervised pipeline that combines markerless point-tracking, spectral analysis, and non-negative tensor decomposition to reduce facial video to a small set of interpretable components. Applied to videos of mice performing Pavlovian conditioning, a brain-machine interface task, and free behavior, face-rhythm recovers whisking, sniffing, licking, and subtler motifs. The resulting components are consistent across animals, decode task variables and internal states, and explain cortical activity with a low-rank representation. Facial motor cortex neurons are predicted well by a phase-invariant spectral transformation of movements above roughly 0.5 Hz, whereas slower movements retain a phase-variant representation. Face-rhythm compares favorably with deep-learning tracking and embedding methods while yielding an interpretable description of facial behavior.

items.title: Which Patients with Advanced Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Benefit Most from First-line Checkpoint Inhibitor Combination Regimens: A Meta-analysis of Individual Patient Data and Aggregate Data from Randomised Trials.

sections.objective: To quantify heterogeneity in the treatment effects of first-line immuno-oncology (IO)-based combination regimens among patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) according to prognosis and potential effect modifiers and to assess which patients benefit most.
sections.methods: Meta-analysis (preregistered in PROSPERO: CRD42023483638) including randomised trials underpinning first-line IO-based regimens recommended in the European Society for Medical Oncology 2024 guidelines using sunitinib as control, with mature overall survival (OS) data available as of November 2023. Individual patient data (IPD) were obtained for two trials and aggregate data for two others. Prognostic stratification was performed by the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium (IMDC) model and, for IPD trials, by the Clinical Prognostic Index in the Checkpoint Inhibitor era (CPI2) model. Effect modification by sex and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was assessed. OS benefit was summarised as a hazard ratio (HR) and, in IPD, as the difference in restricted mean survival time (dRMST), and was pooled across trials using fixed-effects inverse-variance-weighted models.
sections.conclusion: IO-based regimens showed highly divergent OS efficacy across prognostic subgroups, with no significant benefit among patients with a favourable prognosis and the strongest benefit in patients with a poor prognosis.
sections.other: CheckMate-214, CheckMate-9ER, KEYNOTE-426 and CLEAR were included, totalling 3320 patients (IPD for CheckMate-214 and CheckMate-9ER; n = 1747). Among IPD studies, 42%, 32%, and 26% of patients had CPI2 favourable, intermediate, and poor prognosis, respectively. The respective pooled subgroup dRMSTs were 1.21 (95% CI = -0.82 to 3.25), 3.15 (0.50 to 5.81), and 7.36 (4.56 to 10.17) mo. Using all four studies, the pooled HRs for IMDC favourable, intermediate, and poor subgroups were 0.98 (0.81 to 1.19), 0.78 (0.68 to 0.89), and 0.51 (0.40 to 0.65), respectively. PD-L1 expression at 5% significantly modified the treatment effect.

keywords: Advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma

items.title: Twelve-month great saphenous vein (GSV) occlusion after non-invasive extracorporeal high-intensity focused ultrasound.

sections.objective: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) is a non-invasive extracorporeal thermal ablation technique for superficial venous insufficiency. This study evaluated the 12-month efficacy and safety of HIFU for great saphenous vein (GSV) insufficiency.
sections.methods: VEINRESET was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm pivotal clinical study conducted at four centers, two in Europe and two in the United States. Adults with symptomatic primary GSV insufficiency (Clinical, Etiology, Anatomy, and Pathophysiology class C2 or higher) and duplex-confirmed reflux underwent one extracorporeal HIFU procedure. Low-volume, non-tumescent local anesthetic infiltration was permitted but not required. The primary endpoint was GSV occlusion at 12 months, defined as duplex-confirmed closure along the treated segment with no patent segment exceeding 5 cm, tested against a prespecified 75% performance goal using a one-sided exact binomial test. Secondary endpoints included reflux abolition, revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), visual analog scale (VAS) pain, and safety.
sections.results: Seventy participants underwent treatment, and 68 completed 12-month follow-up. Occlusion was observed in 66 of 68 participants with 12-month duplex data (97.1%), and the imputed 12-month GSV occlusion rate in the intention-to-treat population of 70 participants was 96.8% (95% confidence interval, 88.3-99.2; p = 0.001). The absence of reflux was maintained in 67 of 68 participants (98.5%). At 12 months, mean rVCSS improved from 6.7 ± 2.8 at baseline to 0.5 ± 0.7, and VAS pain score (0-100) decreased from 38.4 ± 14.9 to 0. Most participants resumed normal activities on the treatment day. One mild, nonserious skin numbness event resolved within 2 days.
sections.conclusion: Extracorporeal HIFU achieved high 12-month GSV occlusion, sustained reflux abolition, clinical improvement, and few adverse events in individuals with GSV insufficiency.

items.title: Home and Workplace Secondhand Smoke and Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer Thinning in Never-Smokers: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.

sections.objective: To examine the association of home and workplace secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure with circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness, macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness, and glaucoma among lifetime never-smokers.
sections.methods: Cross-sectional, nationwide population-based study. A total of 4,276 lifetime never-smokers (354 with SHS exposure and 3,922 without SHS exposure) from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2019-2021. Self-reported SHS exposure at home or in the workplace was the primary exposure. cpRNFL and macular GCIPL thicknesses were measured using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography, and glaucoma was centrally adjudicated according to the International Society of Geographical and Epidemiological Ophthalmology criteria. Survey-weighted linear and logistic regression analyses were performed to investigate the associations of SHS exposure with cpRNFL thickness, macular GCIPL thickness, and glaucoma. Trends across the number of exposure settings were also evaluated.
sections.results: Compared with unexposed never-smokers, SHS-exposed participants were younger (47.0±13.1 vs. 49.0±14.0 years, standardized mean difference [SMD]=-0.144), had a greater intraocular pressure (15.1±2.3 vs. 14.9±2.3 mmHg, SMD=0.106), deeper anterior chamber (2.79±0.32 vs. 2.74±0.32 mm, SMD=0.155), and a thinner global cpRNFL (93.0±9.9 vs. 94.4±9.9 µm, SMD=-0.145), whereas axial length, macular GCIPL thickness, and glaucoma prevalence (4.4% vs. 3.4%, SMD=0.054) did not differ. After full adjustment, SHS exposure was associated with thinner global cpRNFL (β=-1.826, 95% confidence interval [CI]=-3.082 to -0.570, P=0.004), with a significant trend across the number of exposure settings (P for trend=0.003). In sectoral analyses, thinner cpRNFL was observed in the inferior (β=-3.003, P=0.006) and temporal (β=-1.429, P=0.012) sectors, which remained significant after Bonferroni correction. Exposed never-smokers had higher odds of belonging to the thinnest cpRNFL quartile (odds ratio=1.485, 95% CI=1.081 to 2.039, P=0.015). Average macular GCIPL thickness (P=0.617) and glaucoma (P=0.170) were not significantly associated with SHS exposure.
sections.conclusion: SHS exposure was associated with cpRNFL thinning in lifetime never-smokers, but not with macular GCIPL thickness or glaucoma. These findings suggest a subclinical structural vulnerability of the cpRNFL to SHS exposure and underscore the public health imperative of reducing SHS exposure to protect ocular neuroaxonal health in never-smokers.
sections.other: cpRNFL thickness, macular GCIPL thickness, and glaucoma.

items.title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair.

sections.objective: To describe contemporary outcomes as well as temporal trends of in-hospital mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) across indications and levels of urgency, establishing a benchmark for future analytic efforts.
sections.methods: The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications. Analyses were stratified by indication to include descending thoracic aortic aneurysms (DTAA), dissections, and trauma. Aneurysms involving the aortic arch (i.e. landing zone 5) were excluded. Linear regression and the Cochran Armitage test for trend were used to analyze yearly mortality and complication rates over time. Mortality and complication end-points were further analyzed using logistic regression with and without risk-adjustment.
sections.results: Over the ten-year study period, 4,632 TEVARs were performed for DTAA, 6,701 for dissection, and 2,321 for trauma. For patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA, in-hospital mortality declined significantly for both elective (2014, 3.9% versus 2024, 1.0%, -0.26 percentage points per year, p=0.01) and nonelective cases (2014, 16.7% versus 2024, 8.7%, -0.63 percentage points per year, p=0.04). There was also a decline in in-hospital mortality among elective dissection patients (2014, 3.7% versus 2024, 0.5%, -0.17 percentage points per year, p=0.03). Elective TEVAR overall is associated with a mortality rate of less than two percent per year. The in-hospital complication trends declined significantly for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA - elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -1.13 percentage points per year (2014, 24.8% versus 2024, 11.5% p<0.001) and non-elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -2.0 percentage points per year (2014, 40.5% versus 2024, 25.2%, p<0.001). Dissection patients undergoing elective repair had a decrease of -0.8 percentage points per year (2014, 16.9% versus 2024, 9.2%, p<0.001). Nonelective dissections repairs had a complication rate of 36.4% in 2014 vs 34.1% in 2024, p=0.874). Trauma patients tended toward higher complication rates over time, with a rate of 21.6% in 2014 and 32.2% in 2024, p=0.06) Trauma patients experienced an overall increase in in-hospital mortality of +0.38 percentage points per year (2014, 9.8% versus 2024, 9.4%, p=0.01).
sections.conclusion: Temporal trends within the VQI demonstrate improvements in mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA and elective dissection repair, with contemporary yearly mortality rates of less than two percent. Patients undergoing non-elective dissection repair and those with traumatic indications represent challenging and complex pathologies requiring further research to identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

items.title: Final 5-year results of the Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis Feasibility Trials for Treatment of Aortic Arch Aneurysms.

sections.objective: To report final 5-year outcomes from prospective multicenter feasibility studies of the GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) for aneurysms involving the proximal descending thoracic aorta and aortic arch (zones 0-2).
sections.methods: Forty consecutive patients (23 male; mean age, 74±10 years) were enrolled at six sites in prospective, nonrandomized feasibility trials (2014-2016). Patients underwent TEVAR with proximal TBE in zone 0/1 (n=9; NCT02264977) or zone 2 (n=31; NCT02021812). A clinical events committee adjudicated aneurysm-related and all-cause mortality, major adverse events, and cerebrovascular events. Core laboratory analysis assessed endoleaks (types I-IV), aneurysm sac enlargement, device migration, and side branch patency. Five-year cumulative risk rates (2006 days) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
sections.results: The median follow-up time among survivors was 60.2 months (range, 25.8 to 66.0), with 17 patients completing the required 5-year clinical and imaging follow-up across both studies. Eleven late deaths occurred; KM-estimated cumulative risk of 5-year all-cause mortality was 29% (95% CI: 17%-46%). One zone 2 death was adjudicated as aortic-related (2.5%; 95% CI: 0.4%-16%) due to ascending aortic rupture, with no ruptures occurring within treated aortic segments. Reintervention risk through 5 years was low (KM-estimated cumulative risk, 5.1%; 95% CI: 1.3%-19%), with two events, both in the zone 2 cohort. Five patients experienced stroke events through 5 years, corresponding to a KM cumulative risk of 19.0% ( 95% CI: 7.2%-43%), two in zone 2 and three in zone 0/1. Two patients had target vessel instability (5.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-16.9%). Two side-branch patency events occurred in zone 2: one complete side-branch occlusion in the LSA associated with transient mild arm claudication and one asymptomatic partial occlusion, primary patency through 5-year follow-up was 94.8% (37/39 evaluable patients). Core laboratory identified endoleaks in 12 patients (30.8%; 95% CI: 15%-45%). Three patients (7.7%) had a type I or III endoleak by 5 years, all in the zone 2 arm; these included type IA in one patient (2.6%) and type III in two patients (5.1%). Additionally indeterminate (n=8, 20.5%) and type II (n=6, 15.4%) endoleaks were observed. Cumulative risk rate of aneurysm sac enlargement through 5-years was 15.0% for all patients (95% CI: 5.6%-30.3%), with events occurring in three zone 2 patients and one zone 0/1 patient.
sections.conclusion: At 5 years, the early feasibility studies demonstrated excellent side branch patency, a low incidence of type IA endoleak, low aortic-related mortality, and no rupture within the treated aortic segments. Larger studies are needed to better define zone-specific cerebrovascular risk and long-term durability.

items.title: Percutaneous Versus Surgical Access for Transfemoral TAVR: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Vascular Complications.

sections.objective: To compare vascular complications between percutaneous and surgical access during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (tf-TAVI) and estimate pooled outcomes following percutaneous access.
sections.methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative and single-arm studies.
sections.results: Ten comparative studies (4 736 patients) and eight single-arm studies (5 113 patients) were included. Major vascular complications did not differ significantly between percutaneous access and surgical cutdown (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.61-1.14; I2 = 41.8%; 95% prediction interval 0.39-1.78), with no significant differences in secondary clinical outcomes, including hospital length of stay (mean difference -0.96 days, 95% CI -2.38 to 0.47; p = .19). In the single-arm analysis, pooled major vascular complications after percutaneous TAVI were 5.20% (95% CI 3.52-7.63%; 95% prediction interval 1.43-17.21%; I2 = 91.1%), with 30-day mortality of 2.20% (95% CI 1.41-3.40%; 95% prediction interval 0.72-6.46%; I2 = 66.9%). Funnel plot asymmetry (Egger's p = .034) was attributable to a single zero-event study and was not confirmed by the Peters test (p = .651) or after its exclusion (p = .164).
sections.conclusion: Percutaneous femoral access was not associated with a statistically significant difference in major vascular complications or other clinically relevant outcomes compared with surgical cutdown in anatomically suitable patients treated at experienced centres; residual confounding cannot be excluded, and this evidence is largely observational and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending confirmation in randomized trials.
sections.other: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 8 July 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261454909). Comparative (odds ratio [OR]) and single-arm (pooled proportion) random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Subgroup, meta-regression, sensitivity, and publication-bias analyses were conducted for the primary outcome. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I, ROBINS-I Single Arm, and RoB 2.

items.title: Incidence of Aortic Vascular Graft and Endograft Infection in Patients with Bloodstream Infection - A Population-Based Study.

sections.objective: To assess incidence and predictors of vascular graft and endograft infection in patients with prior aorto-iliac graft surgery and concurrent blood stream infection.
sections.methods: A population-based observational study was conducted in Skåne, Sweden, between 2010-2022. Patients with prior aorto-iliac graft or endograft surgery were identified in the Swedish Vascular Registry and linked to local blood culture data. Electronic medical records were reviewed according to a predefined protocol and vascular graft and endograft infection was assessed using MAGIC-criteria. Fine-Gray models were used to evaluate predictors of vascular graft and endograft infection diagnosis within three months of a bloodstream infection episode.
sections.results: A total of 418 patients were identified with 569 bloodstream infection episodes. Of 569 bloodstream infection episodes, 83% (n=473) occurred in men and mean age was 74.9 ± 9 years. The 3-month incidence of vascular graft and endograft infection diagnosis was 7.5%. Elevated C-reactive protein at bloodstream infection onset (sHR; 1.004, 95% CI 1.002-1.007, p<.001) and prior urgent aorto-iliac index surgery (sHR 2.77, 95% CI 1.31-5.87, p=.007) were positively associated with vascular graft and endograft infection. C. albicans (sHR 3.97, 95% CI 1.3-12.1, p=.02), Actinomycetales (sHR 8.29, 95% CI 2.3-29.84, p=0.001), L. monocytogenes (sHR 18.22, 95% CI 11.21-29.63, p <.001) or S. aureus (sHR 1.98, 95% CI 1.05-3.72, p=.03) bloodstream infections were positively associated with vascular graft and endograft infection.
sections.conclusion: The 3-month incidence of vascular graft and endograft infection diagnosis after bloodstream infection was 7.5%. Clinical suspicion of vascular graft and endograft infection should be higher in patients with prior urgent aorto-iliac surgery, markedly elevated levels of C-reactive protein at index culture, or bloodstream infection with S. aureus, Actinomycetales, L. monocytogenes or C. albicans.

items.title: Imaging After Retinal Artery Occlusion Versus Transient Ischemic Attack.
items.abstract: Among 3695 matched pairs with same-date emergency department contact, retinal artery occlusion was associated with lower brain imaging use (77.3% versus 91.7%) and slightly higher cervical imaging use (81.7% versus 79.2%) than transient ischemic attack.

items.title: Noncoding functions of FMR1 transcript in riboregulation of human neurodevelopment.
items.abstract: The noncoding functions of protein-coding messenger RNAs (mRNAs) are largely ignored. Here, we demonstrate an unexpected noncoding role of FMR1 mRNA in human neurodevelopment. A loss of FMR1 and its protein product, fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP), leads to the neurodevelopmental disorder fragile X syndrome (FXS). Neurons derived from FXS patients display hyperexcitability and immature morphology, whereas FMRP knockout (FMRP-KO) neurons that retain FMR1 transcript expression do not. Multi-omics analyses reveal key metabolic differences between FXS and FMRP-KO neurons. Although both FXS and FMRP-KO neurons exhibit reduced mitochondrial respiration, only FXS neurons exhibit elevated glycolysis. We further discover that the FMR1 transcript riboregulates the levels of the glycolytic enzyme lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) by inhibiting the binding of LDHA mRNA to insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 2 (IGF2BP2). Finally, the FMR1 transcript, independent of FMRP, rescues glycolytic and cellular deficits of FXS neurons. Together, these results suggest that FMR1 is a dual-function RNA in human neurodevelopment.

items.title: Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation: PRIME-MR Registry Insights.

sections.objective: Sex-related differences have been previously explored in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) undergoing surgery as well as those with secondary MR treated with transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). This study sought to evaluate sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TEER for primary MR.
sections.methods: Outcomes of Patients Treated with M-TEER for Primary MR (NCT05332782) is an international, retrospective registry including patients undergoing TEER for primary MR in 27 centers. The primary outcome was a composite of 2-year all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization.
sections.results: A total of 2,078 patients, including 961 (46.3%) females, were analyzed. Females were older and had fewer comorbidities but presented with a different anatomy and more advanced symptoms. Compared with males, females were more frequently excluded from surgery because of advanced age and frailty. Optimal procedural results were lower in females, with a higher incidence of residual MR ≥2+ (38.5% vs 32.1%; P = 0.0037), and a significantly higher mean transmitral gradient (4.0 vs 3.6 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality in female patients. In contrast, the incidence of the primary composite endpoint, as well as heart failure hospitalization alone, did not differ significantly. After adjusting for comorbidities, females demonstrated lower primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.77; P = 0.009), lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.62; P < 0.001), and lower cardiovascular mortality (subdistribution HR: 0.53; P = 0.011).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with primary MR, females were older and presented with a different clinical and anatomical profile compared with males. Although optimal procedural results were lower in females, higher survival rates in females vs males suggest that mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be a good option regardless of sex.

items.title: Clinical Course of Faricimab-Induced Intraocular Inflammation: A J-CREST Study.
items.abstract: Faricimab-induced intraocular inflammation is rare (0.47% per patient; 0.090% per injection) and manifests as anterior-limited inflammation or intermediate uveitis. Although intermediate uveitis causes greater visual decline, appropriate corticosteroid treatment achieves visual recovery.

items.title: Early food introduction and skin intervention in the prevention of food allergy in young children (PreventADALL): 7-year follow-up of a factorial, multicentre, cluster-randomised trial.

sections.objective: In our previous study, early food introduction prevented food allergy, whereas skin intervention alone did not prevent atopic dermatitis at age 3 years. In this follow-up study, we aimed to determine the effect of food and skin interventions on food allergy, allergic sensitisation, atopic dermatitis, food avoidance diets, and BMI at age 7 years.
sections.methods: We conducted a 7-year follow-up study of 2394 children from Norway and Sweden antenatally included (between Dec 9, 2014, and Oct 31, 2016) in the ongoing, general-population-based Preventing Atopic Dermatitis and ALLergies in children (PreventADALL) study. Children were randomly assigned at study site hospitals at birth (1:1:1:1) into the 2×2 factorially designed cluster-randomised controlled trial to no intervention (n=597), skin intervention (n=575; oil baths and facial cream from age 2 weeks to 9 months a minimum of four times weekly), food intervention (n=642; tastes of peanut, cow's milk, wheat, and egg a minimum of four times weekly from ages 3-6 months), or both interventions combined (n=583). The primary outcome at the 7-year follow-up was allergy to any of the interventional foods, as diagnosed by an expert panel following international guidelines. Secondary outcomes were allergy to the individual interventional foods, allergy to non-interventional foods, allergic sensitisation by skin prick test and serum-IgE, atopic dermatitis by validated diagnostic criteria, food avoidance diets through interview, and BMI. Study personnel performing clinical assessments and all researchers involved in data analysis were masked to group allocation, except for the data manager for some parts of the analysis. Mixed logistic regression with best case imputation (of no atopic disease) was used to estimate risk differences. The trial is registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT02449850) and is closed for recruitment.
sections.results: At the 7-year follow-up, the risk of food allergy to interventional foods (38 [1·6%] of 2394) was similar in the no food intervention (21 [1·8%] of 1170) versus food intervention groups (17 [1·4%] of 1224; risk difference -0·4% [95% CI -1·4 to 0·6]). Any food allergy was diagnosed in 76 (3·2%) of 2394 children, similar across the intervention groups. Allergic sensitisation to interventional foods at 7 years was lower in the food intervention (67 [9·9%] of 680) versus no food intervention groups (95 [15·6%] of 610; -5·7% [-9·3 to -2·1]). Atopic dermatitis was less frequent in the combined intervention group (17·3%) than in the controls (25·2%; -7·8% [-12·5 to -3·2]). Food avoidance diets and BMI were similar across the intervention groups.
sections.conclusion: Early short-term food intervention was insufficient for sustained food allergy prevention by age 7 years, despite reduced allergic sensitisation, suggesting that continued allergen exposure might be needed for long-term prevention. Combined food and skin interventions reduced atopic dermatitis at 7 years.

items.title: Genome-directed treatment targets and mutational signature biomarkers: a retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis.

sections.objective: The clinical application of precision oncology therapies is currently restricted to selected cancer cases harbouring highly specific mutations. Targeted therapies are typically approved for use in specific tumour types in which these alterations occur frequently. We aimed to systematically catalogue targetable alterations and genome-wide biomarkers across all solid tumour types to identify additional therapeutic opportunities.
sections.methods: In this retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis, for the primary cancer cohort, we used matched fresh frozen tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a discovery cohort of 11 013 tumours comprising 19 tumour types collected from 10 334 participants in the UK-based 100 000 Genomes Project (100kGP). Participants were recruited to this cohort through 13 National Health Service Genomic Medicine Centres or hospitals affiliated to the 100kGP between 2012 and 2019. For the metastatic cancer cohort, we used matched tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a cohort of 6016 solid tumours collected from 5658 patients from the Netherlands who contributed to the Hartwig Medical Foundation (HMF) database (accessed Aug 19, 2025). Snap-frozen tumour DNA and matched normal DNA from blood samples underwent whole-genome sequencing. Potentially targetable alterations, comprising (1) immediately actionable alterations, (2) investigational alterations, and (3) mutational signature-informed features, were sought in all samples. The primary outcome of this study was to assess the pan-cancer frequency and tissue distribution of potentially targetable alterations.
sections.results: Between July 1, 2025, and March 3, 2026, we analysed samples from 17 029 tumours from the 100kGP and HMF cohorts. Immediately actionable alterations were identified in 2081 (18·9%) of 11 013 primary and 1559 (25·9%) of 6016 metastatic cancers; a further 1204 (10·9%) primary and 867 (14·4%) metastatic cancers harboured investigational alterations or mutational signature-informed features. 2914 (51·1%) of the 5706 immediately actionable variants identified were found in tumour types where the biomarker is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Although some immediately actionable alterations (including gene-fusion targets and MET exon 14 skipping variants) were restricted to fewer tumour types, most immediately actionable alterations (including HER2 amplification, RAS-RAF pathway alterations, IDH1 mutations, and DNA repair deficiencies) occurred across multiple tumour types, frequently beyond those for which matched targeted therapies are currently approved. Mutational-signature biomarkers of DNA repair or replication deficiencies were similarly observed across tumour types. Metastatic cancers, including rare and moderately rare tumour types and cancers of unknown primary, harboured a notably high prevalence and diversity of targetable events.
sections.conclusion: Our findings support comprehensive whole-genome sequencing assessment of cancers irrespective of tumour type. Prospective clinical trials are required to establish whether therapeutic vulnerabilities identified by whole-genome sequencing can extend the effective use of targeted therapies beyond their current tumour-specific indications.

items.title: Surgical Management of Thoracic Aortic Mural Thrombus: Operative Strategy and Early Outcomes in a Two-Decade Retrospective Single-Center Experience.

sections.objective: Thoracic aortic mural thrombus (TAMT) is a rare but life-threatening condition due to the risk of systemic embolization. In this single-center retrospective surgical case series, we evaluated perioperative management, operative strategy and outcomes after surgical thrombectomy for TAMT, a condition with limited evidence and no established treatment standard.
sections.methods: Between 2004 and 2025, 14 patients (median age 57.5 years; 9 male) underwent open thrombectomy for TAMT at our institution. TAMT was defined as an intraluminal, imaging-confirmed thrombus attached to a non-aneurysmal and non-dissected aortic wall without identifiable cardiac or proximal embolic source.
sections.results: Acute systemic embolization represented the first clinical manifestation in the majority of patients, including stroke (n = 6), limb ischemia (n = 6) and visceral ischemia (n = 2). Thrombus localization included the ascending aorta (n=1), aortic arch (n=6), combined ascending aorta and arch (n=5), arch and descending thoracic aorta (n=1), and multiple thoracic aortic levels (n=1). All procedures were performed under cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest allowing complete thrombus removal in all patients. One patient died within 30 days in hospital due to sepsis. Two disabling postoperative strokes and one new postoperative peripheral embolic event occurred. Median follow-up time was 3.5 months (IQR 0.4-60.7). No persistent or recurrent TAMT was observed during imaging follow-up (median imaging follow up 0.6 months).
sections.conclusion: Open surgical thrombectomy with hypothermic circulatory arrest permitted complete macroscopic thrombus removal in this selected surgical cohort and was technically feasible.

items.title: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.

sections.objective: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete.
sections.results: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups).
sections.conclusion: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes.

items.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
sections.methods: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).
sections.conclusion: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

items.title: 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan.

sections.objective: Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.
sections.methods: PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.
sections.conclusion: A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

items.title: Ambient scribes as narrative technologies.
items.abstract: Ambient scribes, also known as artificial intelligence-powered voice-to-text technology, are widely cited as time-saving tools that reduce administrative burden for clinicians. Yet, in their current use, these tools pose substantial, often unacknowledged risks that threaten to undermine patient-centred care. We argue that ambient scribes are inherently narrative technologies whose risks-and potential benefits-cannot be fully understood without careful attention to the ways that patients tell their stories and the broader context in which those stories are told. Drawing on medical humanities scholarship, we show that current approaches to ambient scribes take a superficial approach to narrative interpretation that omits the clinically relevant aspects of patient experience. We propose three ways to integrate more robust narrative analysis that can increase the value of ambient scribes: centring patient perspectives, accounting for material and social structures that shape narrative, and reframing the clinical encounter as a node in a broader narrative system. We conclude by outlining five priorities for commissioners, administrators, clinical leaders, and practice managers to ensure that the roll-out of ambient scribes does not deepen existing harms, and could instead contribute to more humane and trustworthy care.

items.title: Empirical treatment with valganciclovir in infants living with HIV and hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa: a multicentre, open-label, factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high. This trial (EMPIRICAL) tested whether empirical valganciclovir treatment for cytomegalovirus improves survival in infants in Africa.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2 × 2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity to receive standard of care (SOC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SOC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SOC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, assessed at day 15 and over 1-year follow-up in the intention-to-treat population. In this Article, we report results for the valganciclovir comparison groups. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03915366 and is complete.
sections.results: From March 15, 2020, to Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were included in the analyses, with 276 allocated to valganciclovir groups (140 valganciclovir; 136 valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and 282 to groups without valganciclovir (142 SOC; 140 tuberculosis treatment). The median patient age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4), and 274 (49%) were female. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and tuberculosis treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·73-1·95], heterogeneity p=0·48). At day 15, 64 (23%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir group and 76 (27%) of 282 in groups without valganciclovir died (rate ratio 0·81 [95% CI 0·61-1·08], p=0·15). 24 (9%) of 276 participants and 13 (5%) of 282, respectively, were lost to follow-up. After 12 months, 119 (43%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir groups and 134 (48%) of 282 in the groups without valganciclovir died (0·88 [95% CI 0·74-1·05] p=0·15). In a time-varying effects model, at day 15, the adjusted hazard ratio of death was 0·60 (95% CI 0·41-0·87, p=0·0063), and their hazard of death over 1 year was 0·79 (0·62-1·01; p=0·068), or 0·76 (0·58-1·00; p=0·0500) when excluding deaths within 48 h of treatment. Severe adverse events during follow-up were not more common in the valganciclovir treatment groups (odds ratio 0·64 [95% CI 0·35-1·16]).
sections.conclusion: Empirical valganciclovir treatment appeared to be associated with a lower hazard of death in infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia than SOC alone or SOC plus empirical tuberculosis treatment, and there was little evidence of associated harms.

items.title: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.

sections.objective: To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study. Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded. Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use.
sections.results: Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension.
sections.conclusion: Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.
sections.other: Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of co-administered cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each in adults with overweight or obesity (REDEFINE 9): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial.

sections.objective: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 2·4 mg each has shown clinically meaningful bodyweight reductions in global phase 3 studies. Different dosing options might support individual treatment responses and tolerability. We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of once per week subcutaneous cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each or 1·0 mg each versus placebo in participants with obesity or overweight and at least one obesity-related complication.
sections.methods: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial (REDEFINE 9) was conducted across 24 sites in Canada, France, Germany, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older; with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m2 or at least 27 kg/m2 and one or more obesity-related complication; and without diabetes. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1:2:1) centrally, using block randomisation (block size of six) and a web-based system, to receive cagrilintide 1·7 mg plus semaglutide 1·7 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 12 weeks), placebo 1·7 mg plus 1·7 mg (hereafter placebo 1·7 mg each), cagrilintide 1·0 mg plus semaglutide 1·0 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 8 weeks), or placebo 1·0 mg plus 1·0 mg (hereafter placebo 1·0 mg each) for 68 weeks, plus nutrition and physical activity counselling until week 74. All treatments were administered subcutaneously once per week. The coprimary endpoints were relative mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 and proportion of participants reaching a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% at week 68, assessed in the full analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants). Safety was assessed in the safety analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of the study drug). This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06388187 (completed).
sections.results: From June 24 to Oct 30, 2024, 333 participants were assessed for eligibility and 24 were excluded. 309 participants were randomly assigned (full analysis set: 104 assigned to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 103 to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 102 to pooled placebo). 308 participants received at least one dose of the study drug. 291 (94%) of 309 participants completed the study and 254 (82%) were on treatment at week 68. The mean age was 48·0 years (SD 13·6) and mean BMI was 39·1 kg/m2 (6·8). 239 (77%) participants were female, and 70 (23%) were male. For the efficacy estimand, the mean relative change from baseline in bodyweight at week 68 was -20·7% (SE 0·9) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, -21·0% (1·0) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and -2·0% (1·0) with the pooled placebo. Bodyweight reductions were significantly greater with both doses of cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -18·8 percentage points [95% CI -21·5 to -16·0]; p<0·0001 for the 1·7 mg each dose and -19·0 percentage points [-21·8 to -16·2]; p<0·0001 for the 1·0 mg each dose). The proportion of participants reaching bodyweight reductions of at least 5% at week 68 was significantly greater with cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (95·1% [SE 2·7] with the 1·7 mg each dose vs 33·4% [5·6] with placebo, ETD 61·7 percentage points [95% CI 49·5-74·0], p<0·0001; and 96·3% [2·2] with the 1·0 mg each dose, ETD 63·0 percentage points [51·1-74·9], p<0·0001). Adverse events were reported in 102 (99%) of 103 participants receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 98 (95%) of 103 receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 93 (91%) of 102 receiving the placebo. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and gastrointestinal-related. No deaths were reported.
sections.conclusion: Cagrilintide-semaglutide at 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each was superior to placebo at reducing bodyweight in adults with overweight or obesity, suggesting that different dose levels might support treatment flexibility.

items.title: Effects of plastic exposure on human health.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a critical environmental and public health challenge, with growing evidence linking human exposure to microplastics, nanoplastics, and associated chemicals to adverse health outcomes. This review summarises current knowledge on the health effects of plastic exposure, addressing both established findings and critical knowledge gaps. We examine human exposure to plastics and associated health risks based on available clinical and epidemiological evidence. Additionally, we explore chemicals associated with plastic, including their potential as carcinogens and disruptors of endocrine and immune function. Recognising the urgent need for preventive measures, we examine emerging strategies for reducing plastic burdens, including global regulatory efforts like the United Nations Plastics Treaty and proposed public health guidelines. By integrating current evidence, this review aims to provide a foundation for advancing research and informing strategies to mitigate health risks associated with plastic.

items.title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices.
items.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists versus DPP-4 and SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients with Bronchiectasis and Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Bronchiectasis is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited disease-modifying therapies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, but their impact on bronchiectasis outcomes remains unknown.
sections.methods: Using the TriNetX global federated research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between June 1, 2022, and May 30, 2025. We compared clinical outcomes, including all-cause mortality, bronchiectasis exacerbation, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infections, with patients receiving DPP-4i) or SGLT2i using propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics.
sections.results: After propensity score matching, 1,029 patients per group were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i cohort, and 2,255 patients per group in the GLP-1RA versus SGLT2i cohort. Compared with DPP-4i, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.56) and reduced risks of acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.46-0.65). Similar benefits were observed compared with SGLT2i for all-cause mortality (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.40-0.60), acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.39-0.55), and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.68-0.86). Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent mortality benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups, with particularly pronounced effects in obese patients but there was no statistically significant reduction in bronchiectasis exacerbations.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality and reduced respiratory complications compared with DPP-4i or SGLT2i. These findings suggest potential disease-modifying benefits of GLP-1RAs in bronchiectasis beyond glycemic control.
sections.other: Is GLP-1RA use, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, associated with better clinical outcomes in patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes (T2D)?

items.title: The Burden of Chronic Cough in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease: a US Survey-Based Analysis of Its Effects on Daily Life and Emotional and Social Well-Being.

sections.objective: Chronic cough (≥8 weeks) is highly prevalent among patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and imposes significant physical, social, and psychological burden. Research characterizing the burden of chronic cough in patients with IPF and non-IPF ILD from the patient perspective is limited.
sections.methods: An online cross-sectional survey was distributed to adults from June to July 2025 via the Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation's US Community Registry. Eligibility required a self-reported diagnosis of IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough. Multiple-choice and open-text questions spanned six domains: demographics, disease history, cough characteristics, daily life impact, social/emotional and long-term impact, and healthcare experience.
sections.results: A total of 197 participants completed the survey: 75.63% reported a diagnosis of IPF, 21.32% reported non-IPF ILD, and 3.05% were awaiting further ILD diagnosis. Participants reported cough-related interference with daily activities (76.15%) and sleep disruption (79.69%) within the preceding week. Emotional burden was frequently reported: 95.94% of participants had cough-induced worry, 75.13% had depression, sadness, or low mood, and 67.01% reported avoiding social situations because of cough. Additionally, 60.91% of participants reported that chronic cough affected their platonic relationships, and 55.33% reported impact on their ability or desire to maintain physical or intimate relationships. To treat cough, participants reported using an average of 2.7 therapeutic classes historically and 2.0 classes currently, with many reporting limited or no relief.
sections.conclusion: Findings from this US survey of patients with IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough indicate that, among respondents, chronic cough burden manifests physically, psychologically, and psychosocially. Reports of limited relief from available therapies suggest an unmet need in managing chronic cough in this patient population.
sections.other: What is the multidimensional burden of chronic cough in patients living with IPF or non-IPF ILD?

items.title: Single vs. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

sections.objective: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).
sections.results: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect.
sections.conclusion: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy.
