In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

items.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
items.abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

items.title: Personalised mobile health coaching from early pregnancy to 12-months postpartum for females at risk of gestational diabetes (Bump2Baby and Me): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Maternal overweight and obesity increase the risk of gestational diabetes and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Digital health interventions offer scalable, personalised support, but evidence for interventions spanning both pregnancy and postpartum remains scarce. We evaluated the effectiveness of a personalised mobile health (mHealth) coaching intervention for females at increased risk of gestational diabetes.
sections.methods: This multicentre, randomised controlled trial conducted in Australia, Ireland, Spain, and the UK enrolled pregnant females aged 18 years and older between 12-24 weeks of gestation with increased risk of gestational diabetes (Monash GDM risk tool score ≥3; tool risk factors were maternal age, BMI, ethnicity, family history of diabetes, and past history of gestational diabetes). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using computer-generated block randomisation (block size 200; stratified by site) to receive either personalised mHealth coaching via smartphone providing synchronous and asynchronous support through pregnancy to 12 months postpartum alongside usual maternity care, or usual maternity care alone. Usual maternity care, including gestational diabetes screening and management, continued unchanged in both groups, and both groups received Bluetooth-enabled scales. Participants and health coaches could not be masked to allocation; clinical staff providing usual care, laboratory staff, and trial statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was the between-group mean difference in BMI at 12 months postpartum among females at risk of gestational diabetes. The trial was registered at Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Register, ACTRN12620001240932.
sections.results: Between Feb 9, 2021, and Oct 22, 2023, 4386 females were screened, 3521 were excluded, and 865 were randomly assigned (437 to the mHealth intervention group and 428 to the control group). The mean age of participants was 35·2 years (SD 4·3), and most participants were White (588 [73%] of 804). Mean BMI change did not differ between groups (intervention, -0·04 kg/m2 [SE 0·12] vs control, 0·04 kg/m2 [0·13]). Adverse events were recorded in 18% (79 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 25% (106 of 428) of participants in the control group; serious adverse events occurred in 6% (28 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 9% (40 of 428) of participants in the control group. No adverse or serious adverse events were considered related to the intervention.
sections.conclusion: Personalised mHealth coaching spanning pregnancy and an extended postpartum support period did not reduce mean maternal BMI at 12 months compared with usual care. Findings suggest that mHealth interventions targeting at-risk females might benefit from addressing a broader range of maternal health outcomes beyond weight management.

items.title: Geographical targeting of active case-finding for tuberculosis in Pakistan using artificial intelligence software (SPOT-TB): a pragmatic, stepped wedge, cluster-randomised control trial.

sections.objective: Community-wide active case-finding is being increasingly implemented as a tuberculosis elimination intervention. However, conventional site selection strategies can result in low screening yields. We aimed to evaluate whether geographical targeting using artificial intelligence (AI) software can improve detection of tuberculosis during screening in comparison to conventional approaches for site selection, within the programmatic setting in Pakistan.
sections.methods: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped wedge, cluster-randomised trial across all four provinces of Pakistan, and was embedded within The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria-supported active case-finding activities implemented by Pakistan's National TB Control Program and private sector partners. 30 mobile x-ray van teams operating in 68 districts were randomised to transition from conventional site selection approaches (based on field team knowledge, experience, and historical data) to an AI-guided targeting strategy using the Mapping and Analysis for Tailored disease Control and Health system strengthening-Artificial Intelligence (MATCH-AI) software. All individuals attending community active case-finding camps were eligible for participation except those excluded as per the national guidelines. The primary outcome, camp positivity yield, was defined as the number of individuals diagnosed with bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis per camp. The primary analysis was by intention to treat and camps conducted within a 5-km radius of AI recommended locations were included in a validated per-protocol analysis. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06017843, and has been completed.
sections.results: Between Aug 1, 2023, and Sept 28, 2024, 3936 screening camps were conducted (2046 [52·0%] control, 1890 [48·0%] intervention), screening 269 254 individuals. In the intention-to-treat analysis, camp positivity yield was 7% higher in the intervention group, but not statistically significant (adjusted risk ratio 1·07, 95% CI 0·94-1·22; p=0·27). In the validated per-protocol analysis, the camp positivity yield was 32% higher in the intervention group (1·32, 1·12-1·54; p<0·0001). Yields were highest in districts with moderate yields at baseline before the trial and in rural districts.
sections.conclusion: AI-guided targeting was associated with substantially higher detection of bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis during active case-finding in the validated per-protocol analysis and could improve efficiency of community-based tuberculosis case-finding interventions in high burden countries. Routine programmatic data did not capture all implementation or process-quality indicators, limiting assessment of implementation fidelity and variation across sites.

items.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart.
items.abstract: Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45-MCM-GINS) helicase1,2. Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability3-6. Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment4. In human cells, the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress7-10, but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG-PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

items.title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice.
items.abstract: Nuclei in early mammalian embryos undergo epigenetic reprogramming that enables the zygote to develop into a complete organism. Whereas changes in chromatin state during this critical transition period have been extensively studied1-3, changes in the nucleus that houses chromatin remain poorly understood. Here, using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation methods, we find that nuclei attain profound softness and plasticity during the two-cell embryonic stage in mice, facilitating major zygotic gene activation. The prominent nuclear deformability is attributable to the rapid clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope by the autophagy factor LC3. Nuclear stiffening by lamin B1 retention or its overloading results in incomplete activation of zygotic genes and impaired development. However, embryos that maintain nuclear deformability escape from this transcriptional interference. High-resolution microscopy and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization analyses revealed an accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the deformable nuclear envelope. An engineered molecular tether that stiffens the nuclei restricts these nuclear activities and suppresses expression of key zygotic gene activation genes. Together, our study identifies a distinct physical nuclear state that embryos acquire at the beginning of life that supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

items.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene1, and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats2-7, yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals' proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.
items.authors: de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz M

items.title: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.

sections.objective: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial. 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.
sections.results: 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.
sections.conclusion: Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.
sections.other: Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023. The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.

items.title: Changes in pregabalin use and overdose after government interventions and media coverage: retrospective observational study.

sections.objective: To evaluate trends in pregabalin use and overdose in Australia and examine temporal relationships with media coverage (December 2018), prescribing and dispensing restrictions (April 2020), and boxed warnings (February 2021).
sections.methods: Retrospective observational study of dispensing and overdose data, with changepoint, interrupted time series, and latent class analysis.
sections.results: 227 864 people were dispensed 3 441 851 pregabalin prescriptions in the PBS 10% sample and 4871 pregabalin overdose calls were made to the Poisons Centre. Pregabalin use peaked in 2018 before plateauing and declining. Three breakpoints were found in dispensing data, with major decreases in level and slope: December 2018, May 2020, December 2021. The combined rate ratio for dispensing was 0.748 (95% confidence interval 0.700 to 0.800). Compared with the projected historical trend in the absence of interventions (counterfactual), approximately 118 390 (93 960 to 140 940) fewer pregabalin prescriptions were recorded nationally in December 2021, and an ongoing reduction of 0.7% (0.5% to 0.9%) was found each month. All breakpoints were associated with declines in overdose rates, with a combined rate ratio of 0.532 (95% CI 0.406 to 0.695). This reduction corresponded to approximately 41.3 (26.9 to 52.4) fewer pregabalin overdose calls in December 2021 and an ongoing reduction of 1.6% (1.0% to 2.3%) each month. Latent class analysis of 57 744 people dispensed pregabalin in the 12 months after the final breakpoint revealed four groups. The high risk group (7790, 13.5%) were more likely male, younger, dispensed more pregabalin, with shorter refill interval and high rates of opioids and benzodiazepine co-use (5120 (65.7%) and 2455 (31.5%), respectively).
sections.conclusion: Pregabalin use and overdose in Australia have declined in recent years. Major decreases in trend corresponded with media coverage (December 2018) and prescribing and dispensing restrictions (May 2020). The third breakpoint may be a delayed impact of boxed warnings (implemented February 2021). These findings suggest that regulatory and risk communication measures may contribute to reducing pregabalin related harm.
sections.other: Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data (PBS; 10% random sample of people with drug subsidies) and overdose calls (self-harm, recreational use, and misuse) reported to Australia's largest Poisons Centre (50% national sample), 2016-24. Population adjusted rates of dispensing and overdose, timing of breakpoints and rate ratios, proportion of people who use pregabalin at high risk of misuse.

items.title: Trevogrumab (anti-GDF8) with or without garetosmab (anti-activin A) for prevention of muscle loss during semaglutide-induced weight reduction in people with obesity (COURAGE): a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.

sections.objective: Rapid weight loss, as induced by GLP-1 receptor agonists, is accompanied by pronounced muscle loss. GDF8 (myostatin) and activin A (ActA), acting via ActRIIA/B receptors, are negative regulators of muscle mass. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of antibodies blocking GDF8 (trevogrumab) and ActA (garetosmab) on semaglutide-induced weight and muscle loss.
sections.methods: COURAGE is a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial. This multicentre (60 sites), US-based trial enrolled participants aged 18-80 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). In part A, participants were treated for 26 weeks with semaglutide (titrated to 2·4 mg subcutaneously weekly) in addition to a randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) concomitant treatment: placebo, trevogrumab 200 mg, trevogrumab 400 mg, or trevogrumab 400 mg and garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Trevogrumab was administered subcutaneously weekly and garetosmab was administered intravenously every 4 weeks. Part A also included a subsequent semaglutide withdrawal period, at which point participants (randomly assigned at baseline 1:1 within each group) received either trevogrumab 400 mg or placebo for an additional 26 weeks. In part B, participants were treated with semaglutide for 52 weeks and randomly assigned (1:2:2) to concomitant treatment with placebo, trevogrumab 25 mg, or trevogrumab 75 mg. Groups were stratified according to sex, BMI (<35 kg/m2vs ≥35 kg/m2), and participation in an exploratory MRI substudy assessing thigh muscle volume. Study participants, the principal investigators, and study site personnel were masked to all randomisation assignments throughout the study. Primary endpoints were percent change in lean mass, fat mass, and bodyweight from baseline to week 26 (part A) or week 52 (part B). Efficacy and safety analyses were done in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of a study drug (efficacy, as randomly assigned; safety, as treated). COURAGE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299098, and is currently active, not recruiting.
sections.results: 975 participants were enrolled between June 21, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Mean age was 49·0 years (SD 13·2) and mean BMI was 36·7 kg/m2 (SD 5·0); 627 (64%) of 975 participants were female and 348 (36%) were male. In part A (n=605, of whom n=599 received at least one dose of study drug), a substantial decrease in lean mass was observed in the semaglutide plus placebo group at week 26 (-6·6% [95% CI -7·4 to -5·7]); the estimated treatment difference (ETD) versus semaglutide plus placebo was +3·1% (95% CI 1·9 to 4·3) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg, +2·7% (1·5 to 4·0) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg, and +4·5% (3·1 to 5·9) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg. In part B (n=376), lean mass percent change from baseline to week 52 for semaglutide plus placebo was -7·3% (-8·8 to -5·8); the ETD versus semaglutide plus placebo was +1·5% (-0·3 to 3·3) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 25 mg, and +3·1% (1·3 to 4·9) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 75 mg. Change from baseline in fat mass in part A was -15·6% (-17·4 to -13·9) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg group (-3·4% [-5·9 to -0·9]) and the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-11·7% [-14·4 to -9·0]) in part A. No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in fat mass compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Percent change in bodyweight in part A was -10·6 (-11·6 to -9·7) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant for the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-2·7 [-4·1 to -1·2]). No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in bodyweight compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Semaglutide plus trevogrumab (25 mg, 75 mg, 200 mg, or 400 mg) was generally well tolerated with a safety profile similar to semaglutide plus placebo; however, semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg had a high incidence of serious adverse events (14 [9%] of 149) and treatment discontinuations (48 [32%] of 149). Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most commonly reported, and they occurred with similar incidence across treatment groups. Muscle spasms occurred more frequently in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (61 [41%] of 149) compared with the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg or 400 mg groups (23 [8%] of 299) and semaglutide plus placebo groups (seven [5%] of 151). Most adverse events were mild to moderate in severity. Two deaths occurred during the study, both in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group; a causal association between treatment and these events was not identified.
sections.conclusion: This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health.

items.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma.

sections.objective: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety.
sections.results: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered.
sections.conclusion: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

items.title: From surgical video to ophthalmic surgical intelligence: Evidence and translational challenges.
items.abstract: Microscope video provides a rich source of information for artificial intelligence in ophthalmic surgery, but recognition accuracy alone does not establish clinical benefit. We examine video-based workflow understanding, skill assessment, intraoperative assistance, and their potential integration with multimodal sensing and supervised robotic action, with emphasis on cataract and vitreoretinal surgery. Public datasets support retrospective recognition of phases, instruments, anatomy, and selected aspects of technical performance. Early live-use studies suggest possible workflow benefits, whereas patient-outcome evidence remains limited. Video foundation models extend technical capabilities, but porcine-eye navigation results remain surrogate evidence. Small human robotic studies establish feasibility for selected surgeon-controlled tasks, not safety equivalence, clinical superiority, or artificial intelligence autonomy. We propose an unvalidated framework comprising technical validity, external robustness, human factors and workflow, and clinical safety and benefit, assessed independently of the system's permitted level of action. These dimensions are neither a validated scale nor a compulsory sequence. A worked example of live cataract phase assistance illustrates how they identify use-specific evidence gaps without implying that greater autonomy confers greater clinical value. Translation requires independent validation, prospective human-factors evaluation, patient-relevant endpoints, data governance, and post-deployment monitoring. The central question is whether a defined system improves decisions, training, or outcomes under its intended conditions of use.

items.title: Early prediction of surgical site complications after vascular groin incision using postoperative drainage kinetics: A retrospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Groin incisions in vascular surgery are associated with a considerable incidence of postoperative surgical site complications (SSCs), with lymphatic complications such as lymphorrhea and lymphocele representing a frequent and clinically relevant source of morbidity. Previous studies have identified postoperative drainage volume as a potential surrogate marker for impaired lymphatic healing and subsequent wound complications. Based on these observations, researchers have proposed standardized drainage management strategies to help identify high-risk patients early and guide timely intervention. This study retrospectively evaluates postoperative outcomes after implementing this strategy.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective cohort analysis included 106 patients with 114 vertical groin incisions undergoing open vascular procedures requiring femoral exposure between June 2023 and June 2024. We defined SSCs according to a previously published classification. We defined the groin incision as the unit of analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of clinically relevant SSCs (grades 2-4). Secondary outcomes included drainage characteristics, drain removal timing, lymphatic interventions, and risk factors for lymphatic complications.
sections.results: Postoperative drainage volumes were significantly associated with clinically relevant surgical site complications (SSC grade 2-4). Drainage on POD 1 was not significantly associated with complications. Higher drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards were significantly associated with complications, with increasing effect sizes over time (POD 2: OR 1.048, p = 0.022; POD 3: OR 1.047, p = 0.023; POD 4: OR 1.178, p < 0.001). Cumulative drainage up to POD 4 demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (OR 1.024, p = 0.0006; c = 0.831). Overall, 43.0% of groin incisions developed clinically relevant SSC.
sections.conclusion: Postoperative drainage kinetics enable early identification of patients at risk for clinically relevant lymphatic complications after vascular groin surgery. While drainage of POD 1 is not predictive, drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards allow reliable risk stratification with progressively increasing predictive accuracy. POD 2 drainage output is a clinically relevant predictor of subsequent lymphatic complications. A POD2 drainage output ≥80 mL/24 h may support early identification of high-risk patients and facilitate timely interdisciplinary planning of targeted lymphatic interventions.

items.title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.

sections.objective: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis.
sections.methods: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed.
sections.results: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies.
sections.conclusion: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

items.title: Success Rate and Factors Predictive of Redo Endothermal Ablation of Anterior Saphenous Veins (ASV).

sections.objective: Endothermal ablation (ETA), including endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), is commonly used to treat anterior saphenous vein (ASV) insufficiency, previously termed the anterior accessory saphenous vein (AASV). Although less prevalent than great saphenous vein (GSV) reflux, ASV incompetence represents a significant and often under-recognized cause of chronic venous disease. This study evaluates the success of redo ASV ablation and identifies factors associated with recanalization.
sections.methods: A retrospective review was conducted of 16,506 ETA procedures performed in 4,871 patients between 2012 and 2022, which was due to changes in protocol and different device usage in the practice. Of these, 763 ASV ablations were performed in 542 patients with chronic venous insufficiency (CVI). Postoperative duplex ultrasound surveillance was conducted 3-7 days following ablation, every 3-6 months during the first year, and every 6-12 months thereafter. Redo ablation was defined as duplex-confirmed recurrent reflux in a previously treated ASV associated with persistent or recurrent symptoms. Patients were followed at 3-month intervals during the first postoperative year and semiannually thereafter. Redo ablations were performed in patients with symptomatic ASV reflux involving ≥10 cm of vein length.
sections.results: A total of 763 ASV ablation procedures were analyzed, including 552 performed in women and 211 in men; 447 involved the left leg and 316 the right. The cohort was 5% Asian (n = 27), 24% Black (n = 129), 25% Hispanic (n = 138), and 46% White (n = 470). Redo ablation procedures occurred in 29 cases, including 1 Asian, 3 Black, 3 Hispanic, and 22 White patients. Among redo cases, mean age was 63.0 ± 14.7 years, mean BMI was 33.9 ± 9.2 kg/m2, and mean follow-up was 24.5 ± 15.9 months. CEAP classifications for the overall cohort were C2 (n = 26), C3 (n = 276), C4 (n = 320), C5 (n = 14), and C6 (n = 98). EVLA was performed in 316 procedures and RFA in 447. The technical success rate of the index ablation was 92.9% (709/763), compared with 96.6% (28/29) for redo ablations. Older age was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of requiring redo ASV ablation (p = 0.003). No significant associations were observed for BMI, CEAP class, sex, laterality, or ablation modality.
sections.conclusion: Redo ASV ablation is safe and effective, achieving outcomes comparable to primary procedures. These findings underscore the importance of recognizing ASV insufficiency as a major component of CVD and support its appropriate treatment when clinically indicated.

items.title: Acute zonal occult outer retinopathy: Reappraising a historical clinical concept in the era of multimodal imaging.
items.abstract: Acute zonal occult outer retinopathy (AZOOR) and the broader "AZOOR complex" have historically encompassed several disorders sharing acute visual symptoms and outer retinal dysfunction. Advances in multimodal imaging have revealed structural abnormalities in many of these presentations, challenging the original concept of an "occult" retinopathy without a visible anatomical correlate. We therefore revisit these concepts in light of modern imaging and current understanding of outer retinal disease. A systematic reassessment of 207 eligible published cases showed that 188 (90.8%) could be assigned a more specific contemporary diagnostic category based on the information available in the original reports. The most frequent assignments were multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS), acute outer retinopathy (AOR), and multizonal outer retinopathy and retinal pigment epitheliopathy (MORR). These findings do not establish that the original diagnoses were incorrect or that each contemporary diagnosis represents a biologically independent disease, but show that many presentations historically grouped under AZOOR can now be characterized more specifically. We review the clinical features, multimodal imaging findings, natural history, and management of the principal retinal entities identified through this reassessment. We also examine inherited, toxic, autoimmune, paraneoplastic, post-infectious, and other disorders that may produce similar retinal appearances or provide the underlying clinical or etiological setting for these presentations. Rather than proposing a new disease classification, we suggest a pattern-based diagnostic approach in which OCT and fundus autofluorescence form the core imaging assessment, with additional imaging modalities selected according to the clinical presentation and differential diagnosis. Imaging is used to characterize the predominant pattern and anatomical level of retinal injury and, when possible, to identify a more specific retinal diagnosis; clinical history, systemic evaluation, laboratory testing, electrophysiology, and genetic testing can then guide further investigation of its etiological setting or identify a specific alternative diagnosis. This approach allows patients presenting within the broad clinical spectrum historically associated with AZOOR to be characterized at the most specific level supported by contemporary imaging, while recognizing that the biological relationships among these retinal entities remain incompletely understood.

items.title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.

sections.objective: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints.
sections.methods: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively.
sections.results: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%).
sections.conclusion: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.

items.title: Comparative efficacy and tolerability of pharmacological interventions for the acute treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder across the lifespan: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Pharmacological treatment is recommended for obsessive-compulsive disorder. Several options are available, yet little is known on comparative effects of individual medications. We aimed to elucidate the efficacy and tolerability of pharmacotherapy for people with obsessive-compulsive disorder, across the lifespan.
sections.methods: We did a systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing short-term pharmacological interventions for obsessive-compulsive disorder. We searched multiple databases, including MEDLINE, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, for literature on licensed or recommended pharmacological treatments for obsessive-compulsive disorder, without age restrictions, from database inception up to March 11, 2026. We included double-blind, randomised controlled trials with outcomes between 8 and 16 weeks. Two reviewers independently and in duplicate extracted outcomes, with a quality check done by a third reviewer. Primary outcomes were efficacy, defined as change from baseline score, and tolerability, defined as the proportion of participants discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. Separately for children and adolescents (aged 0-17 years) and adults (aged ≥18 years), we calculated standardised mean differences (SMDs) and odds ratios (ORs) with random-effects pairwise and network meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework. People with lived experience of obsessive-compulsive disorder were involved in the entire review process, including protocol development, writing, and interpretation of the findings. The study was preregistered in Open Science Framework (identifier 4V3GS).
sections.results: We included 52 randomised controlled trials with 7316 participants. Nine trials were included for children and adolescents (N=822; median age 12·5 years [IQR 11·6-13·2]; 352 [55%] male and 285 [45%] female among 637 participants with reported sex distribution). 43 trials were included for adults (N=6494; median age 36·4 years [35·0-37·9]; 3105 [49%] male and 3200 [51%] female among 6305 participants with reported sex distribution). Data on ethnicity were reported in 15 (29%) of 52 randomised controlled trials, using inconsistent definitions. In children and adolescents, clomipramine was more efficacious than placebo (SMD -1·19, 95% CI -1·73 to -0·64, CINeMA low), as were sertraline (-0·52, -0·80 to -0·02, low), fluoxetine (-0·43, -0·76 to -0·10, low), and fluvoxamine (-0·39, -0·71 to -0·07, low). Clomipramine was more efficacious than fluoxetine (SMD -0·75, 95% CI -1·39 to -0·11; very low), fluvoxamine (-0·79, -1·43 to -0·16; very low), paroxetine (-0·87, -1·51 to -0·22; very low), and sertraline (-0·87, -1·51 to -0·22; very low). Only sertraline was less tolerable than placebo (OR 4·51, 95% CI 1·36 to 14·96; low). In adults, clomipramine (SMD -0·71, 95% CI -0·88 to -0·54; high), fluvoxamine (-0·63, -0·83 to -0·43; high), paroxetine (-0·51, -0·73 to -0·29; moderate), sertraline (-0·49, -0·70 to -0·28; moderate), escitalopram (-0·43, -0·85 to -0·02; moderate), and fluoxetine (-0·37, -0·6 to -0·08; moderate) were more efficacious than placebo, and clomipramine was more efficacious than fluoxetine (-0·34, -0·65 to -0·04; low). Clomipramine (OR 4·65, 95% CI 3·27 to 6·60; moderate), fluvoxamine (2·73, 1·77 to 4·20; moderate), fluoxetine (2·52, 1·27 to 4·98; moderate), sertraline (2·23, 1·49 to 3·34; moderate), and paroxetine (1·99, 1·36 to 2·93; moderate) were less tolerable than placebo. Clomipramine was less tolerable than all active comparators (OR range 1·70 to 3·50; moderate) except fluoxetine (moderate) and venlafaxine (low).
sections.conclusion: Clomipramine showed the largest estimated efficacy for obsessive-compulsive disorder but had a lower tolerability than SSRIs. The evidence of its superiority over individual SSRIs was more pronounced in children and adolescents. Our findings suggest that the trade-off between efficacy and tolerability should be discussed within an individualised, shared, decision-making framework.

items.title: Longitudinal change in FEV1 in adults with cystic fibrosis treated with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor in France: a prospective observational study.

sections.objective: Without cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators, cystic fibrosis is associated with an accelerated decline in percent predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of approximately 1·5% per year. Although treatment with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) initially increases ppFEV1, little is known about its subsequent effect on ppFEV1 decline. Recent analyses of the extension phases of the phase 3 ETI pivotal studies found no evidence of ppFEV1 decline over 4 years in patients aged 12 years and older who were treated with ETI. The objective of this study was to examine the decline in ppFEV1 in a large, real-world cohort of adults with cystic fibrosis.
sections.methods: Data from adults (aged ≥18 years) with cystic fibrosis and at least one F508del CFTR variant who initiated treatment with ETI between Dec 24, 2019, and Dec 23, 2023, at 31 cystic fibrosis centres included in the French prospective national observational ETI study in adults were analysed over 3 years. Eligible participants were those with at least three measures of ppFEV1 taken within 3 months following ETI initiation and the end of follow-up. The reference ppFEV1 was the highest ppFEV1 reached during the first 3 months of ETI treatment, after which subsequent decline in ppFEV1 was analysed by use of a linear mixed-effects model with random effects to estimate each participant's variation from the population mean.
sections.results: Data from 2321 adults with cystic fibrosis were included in this analysis. 1262 (54·4%) participants were male and 1059 (45·6%) were female. Median age was 29·2 years (IQR 23·1-36·7) and the pre-ETI initiation ppFEV1 was 59·7% (IQR 39·8-79·1). Within the first 3 months following ETI initiation, ppFEV1 increased by a median of 14·5 percentage points (IQR 7·9-22·7). The subsequent mean decline in ppFEV1 was 0·70% (95% CI 0·57-0·83) per year. Importantly, the decline in ppFEV1 was heterogeneous, with 1583 (68·2%) of 2321 participants showing no or limited decline (less than or equal to 1·5% per year). The remaining 738 (31·8%) participants showed a decline of greater than 1·5% per year, with 342 (46·3%) of these participants having a decline of greater than 3·0% per year. In multivariable analyses, the decline in ppFEV1 was greater in participants with a higher ppFEV1 at 3 months after ETI initiation. Treatment with oral azithromycin at 1 year after ETI initiation was associated with a lower risk of having a decline greater than 1·5% per year (relative risk 0·78 [95% CI 0·68-0·90]; p <0·01), as was treatment with inhaled antibiotics (0·81 [0·70-0·94]; p <0·01).
sections.conclusion: These results suggest that approximately a third of adults with cystic fibrosis who are treated with ETI had a persistent decline in ppFEV1. These data emphasise the importance of regular ppFEV1 monitoring and highlight the need to improve current therapeutic strategies to prevent ppFEV1 decline. Proposed strategies could include use of newer CFTR modulators to restore CFTR function more effectively, as well as mucoactive, anti-infective, and anti-inflammatory therapies.

items.title: Safety and efficacy of weekly pemvidutide versus placebo for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (IMPACT): 48-week results from a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, phase 2b study.

sections.objective: Glucagon-GLP-1 dual receptor agonists have shown promise in treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The aim of the IMPACT trial was to assess the effects of one such agent, pemvidutide, in patients with MASH and stage F2 or F3 fibrosis. We previously reported the 24-week primary endpoints of MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement. Here we report the secondary endpoints following 48 weeks of treatment.
sections.methods: IMPACT was a 48-week, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 2b trial in patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH and fibrosis stage F2 or F3. Patients from 83 sites, including academic and community hospitals and private clinical research clinics, in the USA and Australia were randomly assigned (1:2:2) using an interactive web response system to receive once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide (1·2 mg or 1·8 mg), administered without dose titration, or placebo. Patients, investigators, the funder, and all other staff, were masked to treatment assignments throughout the study. The dual primary endpoints of MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis or at least one stage liver fibrosis improvement without worsening of MASH were assessed at week 24. Liver biopsies were not collected at week 48, and only secondary endpoints were assessed at this timepoint. All analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population consisting of all randomly assigned patients. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05989711) and is complete.
sections.results: From July 27, 2023, to Nov 21, 2025, 1557 patients were screened and 212 patients were randomly assigned to pemvidutide 1·2 mg (n=41), pemvidutide 1·8 mg (n=85), or placebo (n=86). Mean age was 53·4 years (SD 12·4), mean BMI was 38·7 kg/m2 (7·8), 123 (58%) patients were female, 89 (42%) were male, and 90 (42%) had type 2 diabetes. At week 48, least-squares mean relative changes in liver fat content were -45·2% (95% CI -56·0 to -34·5; difference from placebo -37·1 percentage points [95% CI -50·6 to -23·5]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -54·7% (-62·3 to -47·1; difference from placebo -46·5 percentage points [-57·7 to -35·3]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and -8·2% (-16·5 to 0·2) in the placebo group. The least-squares mean absolute change in corrected T1 relaxation time was -124·2 ms (95% CI -157·1 to -91·4; difference from placebo -103·8 [95% CI -143·9 to -63·6]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -139·5 ms (-161·7 to -117·3; difference from placebo -119·0 [-151·2 to -86·9]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and -20·5 ms (-44·5 to 3·6) in the placebo group. Least-squares mean changes in alanine aminotransferase were -37·8 IU/L (95% CI -44·5 to -31·1; difference from placebo -27·5 [95% CI -35·8 to -19·2]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group and -37·4 IU/L (-42·1 to -32·7; difference from placebo -27·1 [-33·9 to -20·3]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group versus -10·3 IU/L (-15·2 to -5·4) for the placebo group. Least-squares mean changes in enhanced liver fibrosis score were -0·49 (95% CI -0·71 to -0·28; difference from placebo -0·65 [95 % CI -0·92 to -0·38]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, -0·58 (-0·74 to -0·43; difference from placebo -0·74 [-0·97 to -0·52]; p<0·0001) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and 0·16 (-0·01 to 0·32) for the placebo group. The most frequent pemvidutide-related adverse events were nausea (occurring in nine [22%] of 41 patients in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 35 [41%] of 85 patients in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and 15 [17%] of 86 patients in the placebo group), diarrhoea (five [12%] in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 19 [22%] in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and seven [8%] in the placebo group), and constipation (five [12%] in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, 15 [18%] in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and ten [12%] in the placebo group). No severe or serious adverse events were defined as study medication related. Discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in no patients in the pemvidutide 1·2 mg group, one (1%) in the pemvidutide 1·8 mg group, and three (3%) in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: In patients with MASH, 48 weeks of pemvidutide treatment led to significant reductions in non-invasive tests of MASH inflammation and fibrosis, suggesting continued improvement in liver health. These data warrant the continued investigation of pemvidutide in a phase 3 trial.

items.title: Consensus on the definition, components, and grading of composite postoperative pulmonary complication outcomes (PrECiSIOn): insights from an international Delphi expert panel.
items.abstract: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after surgery and contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality, and health-care burden, and are frequently used as endpoints in clinical studies. However, absence of standardised definitions and heterogeneity in component selection limit comparability across studies and might bias estimates of treatment effects. The Postoperative Pulmonary Complications-Evaluation for Consensus on Standardised Outcomes (PrECiSIOn) study was an international, mixed-method consensus study using a Delphi process to establish a standardised definition of PPCs, determine severity-based ranking of individual components, and define approaches for their assessment. A multidisciplinary panel of experts in PPCs was recruited and candidate PPC components were identified through a focused literature review, structured into domains, and evaluated across iterative Delphi rounds using a seven-point Likert scale, with consensus predefined as ≥75% agreement. Patient and patient care representative perspectives were incorporated through interviews and surveys, and panellists assigned severity weights to components reaching consensus. Input from 44 panellists and five patients and patient representatives informed the prioritisation of clinically meaningful outcomes. Consensus was achieved on a standardised PPC construct comprising components grouped into four domains: symptoms, diagnoses, therapies, and outcomes. Panellists supported the use of routinely collected clinical data and a standardised in-hospital monitoring approach but did not reach consensus on the optimal follow-up period or need for post-discharge surveillance. Severity-based rank ordering enabled hierarchical organisation of PPC components according to their clinical importance, supporting the development of ordinal composite outcomes that account for differences in severity between individual complications. This international consensus-based framework provides a standardised definition of PPCs incorporating severity-based rank ordering, addresses important limitations of existing composite outcomes, and might facilitate more consistent and clinically meaningful evaluation of perioperative interventions. Further work should focus on external validation, implementation in clinical trial analyses, and assessment of applicability across diverse patient populations and health-care settings.

items.title: A blended digital parenting intervention for the prevention of sexual violence, exploitative sex, and maltreatment of children at scale in Tanzania: a cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

sections.objective: Childhood sexual, physical, and verbal violence are global public health priorities, affecting 1 billion children each year. ParentApp integrates sexual violence prevention into WHO-UNICEF's open-access Parenting for Lifelong Health programme, using innovative blended digital delivery. We aimed to test the efficacy of ParentApp in preventing sexual violence and maltreatment against adolescent-aged children and improving preventive mechanisms such as family mental health and adolescent-caregiver relationships.
sections.methods: This cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in 80 Tanzanian sub-wards. Participants were primary caregivers aged 18 years and older and their adolescents (aged 10-17 years). Sub-wards were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either ParentApp (intervention group) or a control WASHApp programme. Clusters were randomly assigned in blocks of six, stratified by urban versus rural location. Statisticians carrying out randomisation and data analysts were masked; it was not possible to mask participants or researchers. Intervention groups received a low-cost Android phone installed with ParentApp, a 12-module offline-first app, with one in-person orientation session and remote support via WhatsApp group chats, at a delivery cost of US$6 per family at scale, or $10 with 20% smartphone provision. Control groups received a low-cost Android phone installed with WASHApp, a 12-module offline-first app for water, sanitation, and hygiene, with one in-person orientation session. The primary outcomes were adolescent sexual violence victimisation and maltreatment and high-risk situations for sexual violence, assessed in all participants irrespective of uptake and engagement at 5 months and 18 months post-baseline. The trial was registered on March 14, 2023, with OSF (https://osf.io/t9fxz) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 11 and Oct 9, 2023, 2692 caregiver-adolescent dyads were screened for study eligibility; 2396 adolescents (1217 [50·8%] female and 1179 [49·2%] male) and 2396 caregivers (1795 [74·9%] female and 601 [25·1%] male) were recruited. 2145 (89·5%) adolescents and 2252 (94·0%) caregivers were retained in the study and included in analyses at 18 months. Adolescent girls in ParentApp clusters had a substantial reduction in past-month sexual violence victimisation compared with those in control clusters (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0·43 [95% CI 0·21-0·86]; p=0·018), with no effect for boys (1·21 [0·59-2·43]; p=0·60). Past-month maltreatment (physical abuse, verbal abuse, and neglect) was lower in ParentApp clusters than in control clusters (adolescent report IRR 0·92 [0·88-0·96]; p<0·0001, caregiver report 0·87 [0·82-0·92]; p<0·0001). Past-month exposure to high-risk situations for sexual violence was lower in ParentApp clusters than in control clusters (adolescent girls IRR 0·87 [0·77-0·97]; p=0·012, adolescent boys 0·85 [0·79-0·91]; p<0·0001, caregiver report 0·81 [0·75-0·88]; p<0·0001). There were no reported adverse events.
sections.conclusion: A low-cost blended digital parenting programme in countries such as Tanzania could simultaneously reduce childhood sexual violence (for girls) and maltreatment and sexual violence risk situations (for girls and boys).

items.title: Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

items.title: Occupational burnout among ophthalmologists: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Occupational burnout threatens clinician well-being, workforce stability, and the quality of patient care, yet its burden in ophthalmology has not been synthesized since 2021. We searched 5 databases from inception through March 13, 2026, and included 24 studies reporting burnout among ophthalmologists, ophthalmology trainees, and ophthalmology-specific health care professionals. Across the 12 studies with extractable prevalence data (n = 2792), the pooled prevalence of burnout was 32.4% (95% confidence interval, 19.0%-49.5%; 95% prediction interval, 3.7%-85.6%), with extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 96.9%). All 9 sensitivity analyses produced estimates between 27.0% and 35.0%. Post hoc prevalence varied most with the operational definition of burnout, from 8.9% when all 3 Maslach dimensions were required to 52.7% when any 1 sufficed. Differences by instrument, career stage, and survey era were not statistically significant, and the numerically higher prevalence among residents largely disappeared after excluding the resident and attending studies with extreme definitions. Dissatisfaction with work-life balance (46.6%) was far more common than job dissatisfaction (20.1%). Women, academic or hospital-based practice, heavy workload, low work control, and inadequate support staff were the correlates reported most consistently. Approximately 1 in 3 ophthalmologists experiences burnout, although certainty is very low. Intervention research remains almost absent.

items.title: Senescence induces clonal failure of hepatocyte plasticity and reshapes regenerative lineages.

sections.objective: Telomere dysregulation is a central driver of cellular senescence and chronic liver disease. Yet how physiological telomeric attrition, rather than uniform telomere loss, leads to hepatic functional decline remains unclear. We therefore investigate how resolvable telomere dysfunction reshapes liver regeneration.
sections.methods: An adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR-based strategy was developed to induce resolvable telomeric breaks in mouse hepatocytes while preserving endogenous telomere maintenance. Clonal dynamics, lineage tracing, and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling were used to characterize senescent hepatocyte behavior during chronic liver injury. Human cirrhotic liver samples were analyzed to assess the relationship between hepatocyte telomere length and intermediate cellular states. An in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte plasticity under telomere stress.
sections.results: Telomere-induced senescence did not substantially impair hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic function, but induced a clonal imbalance shaped by telomerase expression. Lineage tracing and single-nucleus transcriptomics demonstrated that senescent hepatocytes exhibited impaired hepatocyte-to-ductal metaplasia during chronic injury, with limited entry into the dedifferentiated state and failure to fully activate the ductal program. This incomplete transition disrupted epithelial composition and exacerbated the ductular reaction. Analyses of human cirrhotic livers revealed an association between preserved telomere integrity and bipotent hepatocyte states. Furthermore, the in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte dedifferentiation under telomere stress.
sections.conclusion: These findings identify senescence as a barrier to hepatobiliary clonal balance rather than a direct trigger of hepatocyte loss. Telomere dysfunction thereby promotes pathological epithelial remodeling during chronic liver injury.
sections.other: Telomere shortening is a common feature of chronic liver disease, but how it functionally contributes to regenerative failure remains incompletely understood. Our study shows that telomere dysfunction does not simply compromise hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic capacity. Instead, senescence acts as a clonal and lineage-selective constraint that limits hepatocyte plasticity and alters which cells contribute to regeneration. These findings provide a mechanistic link between telomere attrition, loss of regenerative diversity, and progressive liver dysfunction, and suggest that preservation of hepatocyte plasticity may be an important determinant of regenerative capacity in chronic liver disease.

items.title: Advances in retinal cellular imaging: Towards single-cell resolution and functional biomarkers.
items.abstract: Retinal imaging has traditionally described tissue and layer level pathology, whereas direct assessment of individual cells in the living human retina has been limited by ocular aberrations, optical contrast and image analysis constraints. Adaptive optics (AO) has substantially changed this landscape by improving lateral resolution and enabling in vivo visualization of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), ganglion-cell-layer structures, immune cells and microvasculature. This review discusses human retinal cellular imaging across three major AO-enhanced platforms: flood-illumination adaptive optics (FIAO), adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) and adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO). These modalities provide complementary capabilities, including rapid en face imaging, depth-resolved volumetric assessment and flexible confocal, non-confocal and fluorescence-based contrast. Recent progress is also being shaped by faster wavefront correction, wider-field acquisition, compressed multichannel imaging, sensorless AO and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted reconstruction, segmentation and quantification. Beyond optical resolution, molecular labeling strategies are beginning to add biological specificity to retinal cellular imaging. Indocyanine green (ICG) supports AO-assisted assessment of RPE mosaic contrast, annexin V-based Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) provides a molecular readout of retinal cell stress and apoptosis, and curcumin-based imaging has been explored as an experimental retinal amyloid marker in Alzheimer's disease. Together, these advances indicate a shift from high-resolution visualization alone towards cellular and molecular biomarkers of disease activity, progression and treatment response. Further translation will require standardized acquisition, robust automated analysis, multimodal validation and larger prospective studies across devices, disease populations and clinical sites.

items.title: Safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity of a combination of TMB-365 and TMB-380 in people living with HIV suppressed with antiretroviral therapy in the USA: a phase 1b/2a, open-label, dose-escalation study.

sections.objective: Long-acting antibody-based regimens might reduce treatment burden for people living with HIV. We aimed to assess safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity of TMB-365, a CD4-directed monoclonal antibody, combined with TMB-380, a long-acting broadly neutralising monoclonal antibody targeting gp120 CD4-binding site.
sections.methods: In this phase 1b/2a, open-label, dose-escalation study, virologically suppressed adults (aged 18-70 years) living with HIV on stable oral combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) were enrolled from six clinic sites in California, Florida, and Texas, in the USA. In phase 1b, participants received single intravenous doses of TMB-365 plus TMB-380 at either 2400 mg, 3200 mg, or 4800 mg and continued ART for 12-16 weeks. In phase 2a, participants discontinued ART at baseline and received 4800 mg of each antibody intravenously every 8 weeks, three times over 24 weeks, without pretreatment screening. Primary outcomes were safety and pharmacokinetics in phase 1b, and safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity in phase 2a. In phase 2a all treated participants were included in safety and efficacy analyses, except one participant inadvertently dosed after developing an acute medical condition before dosing. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05275998) and is complete.
sections.results: Between July 5, 2022, and Nov 20, 2024, 30 participants (28 male and two female) were enrolled in phase 1b, and 20 male participants were enrolled in phase 2a. In phase 2a, two participants discontinued prematurely, and one was lost to follow-up. No serious or grade 3 or worse adverse events were observed. All treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate. Pharmacokinetic targets were met at week 8 in the phase 1b 4800 mg group. In phase 2a, viral suppression at week 24 occurred in 16 (94%, 95% CI 71-100) of 17 participants in the per-protocol population and 16 (80%, 95% CI 56-94) of 20 participants in the intention-to-treat population. No confirmed virological failures were reported.
sections.conclusion: TMB-365 (4800 mg) plus TMB-380 (4800 mg) every 8 weeks appears safe, might be effective as maintenance therapy in virologically suppressed people living with HIV, and merits further study.

items.title: Risovalisib for PIK3CA-mutated recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
sections.methods: We conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients.
sections.results: Between Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four [4%]). There were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: These results support risovalisib as a potential novel treatment option for PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a rare yet lethal cancer in dire need of additional treatment options. Combination strategies including risovalisib could also be explored to further increase efficacy observed in this study.

items.title: Incidence and predictors of suboptimal functional outcomes despite successful reperfusion in paediatric stroke: a cohort study from the Save ChildS Pro registry.

sections.objective: Successful vessel reperfusion with persistent clinical deficit occurs in 40-60% of adults undergoing mechanical thrombectomy but has never been characterised in childhood stroke. We aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of so-called futile recanalisation, in which the occluded artery is reopened but the patient does not recover good function, in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke.
sections.methods: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023. Patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy and had successful recanalisation (expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [eTICI] grade ≥2b) were included. The primary outcome was suboptimal functional outcome despite successful recanalisation, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score greater than 2 at 90 days, on a scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death) on which 0-2 denotes functional independence; three additional thresholds (mRS score >1, Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure [PSOM] >1·0, and PSOM >0·5) were analysed as sensitivity analyses. Adjusted associations between candidate predictors (age, baseline Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [PedNIHSS] score, baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score [ASPECTS], and final eTICI grade) and each outcome were estimated using Firth-penalised multivariable logistic regression. Save ChildS Pro is registered with the German Clinical Trials Registry (DRKS00018960).
sections.results: 101 patients (54 [53%] males and 47 [47%] females; median age 11·0 years [IQR 6·0-15·0]) had successful recanalisation with 90-day follow-up and comprised the analytical cohort. A suboptimal outcome (mRS score >2) occurred in 18 (18%) of 101 patients. On Firth-adjusted multivariable analysis, lower final eTICI grade was significantly associated with suboptimal outcome (adjusted OR 0·44 [95% CI 0·23-0·84], p=0·012), and younger age was associated in the same direction (0·87 [0·78-0·97] per year, p=0·0098); baseline PedNIHSS score and baseline ASPECTS were not independently associated with a suboptimal outcome. Findings were directionally consistent across the three sensitivity thresholds.
sections.conclusion: In this analysis, 18% of children with successful recanalisation had a suboptimal functional outcome at 90 days, markedly lower than the proportion reported in adults (40-60%). Lower recanalisation quality and younger age were independently associated with suboptimal outcome, whereas baseline PedNIHSS score and ASPECTS had limited prognostic value. These findings highlight the need for longer-term studies and challenge the direct translation of adult prognostic frameworks to paediatric stroke, supporting age-specific approaches. Given the limited event count, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation.

items.title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of antidepressants in the long-term treatment of major depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Major depressive disorder carries high risks of relapse and chronicity, necessitating treatments that achieve and maintain response (sustained response). This study aimed to compare antidepressants on their ability to achieve sustained response, and on acceptability, by synthesising data from randomised controlled trials.
sections.methods: For this systematic review and network meta-analysis, we searched the Cochrane Register, AMED, CINAHL, Embase, LILACS, MEDLINE, MEDLINE In-Progress, PsycINFO, the UK National Research Register, and regulatory agency websites from inception to March 27, 2026. We included double-blind randomised controlled trials that compared any of 21 antidepressants head-to-head or with placebo for long-term treatment (>12 weeks) of adult unipolar major depressive disorder. We included enrichment, non-enrichment, continuation, and continuation-extension designs, and extracted study-level data. We could not derive the sex or gender distribution of participants other than female and did not extract data on race or ethnicity. Primary outcomes were efficacy (sustained response rate) and acceptability (all-cause discontinuation). We synthesised data in random-effects pairwise and network meta-analyses to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs), using fluoxetine as a reference in the ranked forest plots. The primary analysis included head-to-head continuation and continuation-extension design studies. Enrichment design studies were incorporated in the analysis using a chain-of-evidence approach.
